description.narrative: Supports the following illustrative program-funded costs: salaries of US, FSN, and TCN and other staff such as PSCs, RSSAs, PASAs, CASUs working for the US Government managing, administering, and supporting programs and their program-funded benefits such as housing, travel, transportation, education allowances etc; institutional contractors that provide such staff, rent, IT services, the program-funded share of utilities, staff training costs and the cost of developing and administering training programs, equipment and supplies, ICASS, vehicle fuel and maintenance, maintenance contracts, janitorial services, operational unit web page development and maintenance, outreach such as publications and the cost of their preparation (including staff costs), and technical assistance to ensure USG compliance with regulations.

Esta área del programa cubre componentes de diseño de programas y gestión del desempeño y aprendizaje. Esta área apoya la evaluación, los estudios y análisis especiales, la planificación estratégica, el diseño de programas y proyectos, el seguimiento de programas (para incluir estudios de referencia y otras necesidades de recopilación de datos) y actividades que apoyan el aprendizaje, la transferencia de conocimientos y la adaptación de proyectos. La evaluación incluye el examen del estado de un contexto nacional o sectorial para informar el diseño del proyecto, pero no incluye la evaluación de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos (consulte el Área programática PO.3 para obtener una definición de evaluación). Estudios o análisis especiales podrían respaldar la planificación estratégica o de proyectos o incluir investigaciones para el aprendizaje general que no esté necesariamente relacionado con el desempeño de las actividades financiadas por el Gobierno de los Estados Unidos. Esta área programática también puede incluir la preparación de planes estratégicos y otras tareas de programación a corto plazo, la evaluación del potencial de las tecnologías de la información y las comunicaciones para mejorar el desempeño a lo largo del ciclo del programa o la difusión de mejores prácticas y lecciones aprendidas.

The objective of the contract, known as ADVISEAnalytics, Data, Visualization, and Information Servicesis to improve the usage of USAID data and information so that the Agency continues to ensure its development outcomes are supported by evidence.

Higher Education for Development (HED) works in close partnership with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and operates with the advice and counsel of the six major U.S. higher education associations to support the engagement of higher education in development issues worldwide. HED manages innovative partnerships that join U.S. colleges and universities with institutions of higher learning in developing nations. In this way, we support and facilitate the engagement of U.S. higher education in global development.

HED gère des partenariats innovants qui unissent des collèges et universités américains avec des établissements d'enseignement supérieur dans les pays en développement. De cette manière, nous soutenons et facilitons l’engagement de l’enseignement supérieur américain dans le développement mondial.

description.narrative: The Famine Early Warning Systems Network is a leading provider of early warning and analysis on food insecurity. Created by USAID in 1985 to help decision-makers plan for humanitarian crises, FEWS NET provides evidence-based analysis on some 35 countries. Implementing team members include NASA, NOAA, USDA, and USGS, along with Chemonics International Inc. and Kimetrica.

description.narrative: (Turkmenistan): The Together for Health program provides health services educational awareness information to key populations as well as opportunities for youth and others to gain knowledge, skills and confidence to lead healthy lifestyles. The program is increasingly expanding partnerships with local nongovernmental organizations, particularly the National Red Crescent Society, to conduct activities and provide direct services. Youth volunteers continue to be extremely active under the program, and efforts will continue to instill this sense of volunteerism and civic engagement. The program will also continue to cooperate with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

The USAID-funded Balkans Media Assistance Program (BMAP) is a regional media support project in the Balkans focused on strengthening the competitiveness, sustainability, and cooperation of the independent media sector in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. BMAP will aim to make media more competitive in the local and regional marketplaces and strengthen the sustainability of the independent media sector across the region, particularly in the digital space.

Objectives for Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia: USAID’s Balkan Media Assistance Program is making media practitioners in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia more competitive in the local and regional marketplace and strengthening the sustainability of independent media in the region

description.narrative: (Europe and Eurasia Regional): This will be BEP's final year of funding to help the Government of Serbia (GoS) to increase the competitiveness of the Serbian economy by streamlining the business enabling environment, improving public financial management, and strengthening financial markets. Project activities are based on priorities identified by the private sector and the GoS; critical reforms related to labor, construction permitting and inspections have been adopted with assistance from the program, but further systematic assistance and capacity development is critical to ensure the effective implementation of these reforms. At the same time, additional critical legislation, including a pending draft law on non-bank financial institutions is planned that could provide a legislative basis for a viable microfinance system in Serbia; BEP's planned assistance will play a critical role in convening key stakeholders and providing assistance to the legislative development and implementation processes.

Objectives for Serbia: The project is helping Serbia achieve reforms that will: Reduce legal and regulatory burdens on businesses; Improve macroeconomic policy and public financial management; Deepen financial market development and increase access to finance.

description.narrative: Assist special populations which may be vulnerable or at-risk on a temporary or chronic basis whose needs are not addressed under emergency humanitarian assistance or other programs. These include groups such as the disabled; orphans, children and at-risk youth; victims of trafficking; victims of gender-based violence; refugees, returnees, ethnic minorities, internally displaced or other socially excluded groups; the elderly; and female heads of household. Depending on circumstances, services may intend to protect groups; mitigate adverse conditions they face, or to remove barriers to help integrate them into society. Components may include measures to increase the capacity of local service and advocacy NGOs and/or professional social workers; to establish public/private service delivery partnerships as well as family and community focused service models; to establish effective referral networks; to develop appropriate service protocols and methods for screening prospective recipients; or to improve public understanding and sensitivity to the needs of the vulnerable. While services provided should not exclude victims of trafficking in persons, programs designed specifically for this group fall under the Peace and Security Objective under the Transnational Crime Area and the Trafficking in Persons and Migrant Smuggling Element.

title.narrative: Legal Support for Civil Society in Central Asian Republics

description.narrative: Provide technical legal expertise to civil society organizations (CSOs), national governments, and law specialists to promote effective development and implementation of legislation regulating civil society.

Objectives for Kyrgyzstan: Support the adoption of several CSO related laws, including the draft laws on Public Councils at the State Bodies, Charitable Organizations, Social Contracting and others. Provide international comparative examples and technical assistance to government and local partners on CSO legislation and regulatory mechanisms. Provide legal assistance and consultations to CSOs. Institutionalize trainings on CSO legislation and framework. Support indigenous efforts at networking among lawyers. Facilitate CSO/government working groups. Assist with organizing public discussions of draft laws. Build CSO capacity to review and respond to draft laws. Facilitate dialogue between CSOs and governments to develop strategic policy documents

description.narrative: (Kyrgyz Republic): Development through Regional Cooperation (DRC) builds the capacity of civil society organizations (CSOs) in the Central Asian Region to communicate and collaborate in order to effectively engage with their respective governments on all aspects of national and regional debate and policy-making. DRC strengthens the institutional capacity of civil society organizations to promote dialogue and coordination mechanisms among the CSO sector, with a focus on CSOs located in remote and disadvantaged areas and demographic groups in individual Central Asian countries; promotes networking and comparative research at the regional level to increase cooperation over issues of mutual interest, such as the environment, women's issues, anti-trafficking, or economic development; and creates a virtual regional platform that will keep CSOs connected beyond the life of the project, allowing them to share information and tools that can be helpful in their work.

title.narrative: Leader for people living with hiv

description.narrative: Activities (including training) aimed at preventing mother-to-child HIV transmission, including ARV prophylaxis for HIV-infected pregnant women and newborns and counseling and support for maternal nutrition. PMTCT-plus ART activities should be described under ARV Drugs and Adult Treatment. Funding for HIV counseling and testing in the context of preventing mother-to-child transmission can be coded under PMTCT or Counseling and Testing; targets should be included in PMTCT. Early infant diagnosis should be included under Pediatric Care.

description.narrative: The Central Asia "Access to Information" program is a regional program, combining country-specific as well as regional activities for Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan that will increase citizen access to civically-relevant information in order to improve governance outcomes. The program will increase citizen access to civically-relevant information through four complementary objectives:1. Increased regional cooperation to improve the competitiveness of non-state media outlets through content generation and sharing;2. Increased resilience of independent media to survive the impending, treaty-mandated shift to digital broadcasting across Central Asia in 2015;3. Strengthened diversity and professionalism of voices in traditional and "new" media; and4. Improved legal and policy environment for media.

description.narrative: The project will identify and support the creativity and innovation inherent in civil society organizations and communities in Tajikistan in order to achieve institutionalized, permanent and durable reforms on particular good governance topics. The project will support initiatives that originate in civil society in Tajikistan that can lead to long-term impact, manifested in any one of a number of different ways, such as: changes to the legislative or regulatory environment; institutionalization of key reforms; changes in the procedures or internal systems that state bodies use to serve the public; and behavior change.This activity is part of a larger, regional project that is implemented in other countries that are part of the USAID/Central Asia Republics Mission. Please refer to other country-specific Operational Plans for details on activities in those countries.

description.narrative: ICNL will draw upon its relationships, partnerships, and expertise to implement the Enhanced Enabling Environment Program (E3 Program). Over the course of the program, ICNL expects to promote an enabling legal framework for civil society in the CARs, thereby supporting a more vibrant and sustainable democratic culture in the region. Specifically, the following results are expected to be achieved:1. Government actors and Civil Society Organisations are able to improve the legal enabling environment. 2. The improved capacity of CSOs and government to translate law into practice through proper implementation. 3. The increased awareness of CSOs of their rights and responsibilities under the law so that they can more effectively advocate for their rights and comply with their legal obligations.

title.narrative: Economic and Social Connections: A Multi-Input Area Development Financing Facility for Tajikistan (ESCoMIAD)

description.narrative: (Tajikistan): This activity strengthens regional stability and growth by promoting sustained improvements in the quality of life for people living along the Tajik border with Afghanistan helping the communities to become more resilient to shocks, ultimately helping both countries on their pathway to self reliance. In FY 2019, ESCoMIAD's final year, the project will continue its activities across multiple sectors including increasing the profitability of new and existing microenterprises, enhancing access to financial services, and improving health and education services. Specifically the activity will wrap up its support of the more than 40 micro-enterprises and 200 community-based savings groups created since the activity's inception. This program is a Global Development Alliance (GDA) with one to one match where USAID and Aga Khan Foundation are contributing $6 million U.S.D. each. These efforts will contribute to the USAID/State Department's Joint Strategic Plan Mission Objective 3.1: Promote Tajikistan's competitiveness in regional and international markets..

description.narrative: As part of a regionally-managed water resources project, selected river-basin management organizations on both sides of cross-border rivers and water basins will receive assistance for the preparation of their own annual basin management plans. Water basin organization members receive training and technical assistance as they move through the plan in order to learn how to conduct it step by step. Coordinated management of shared water resources is fostered between basin-management organizations on both sides of the cross-boundary rivers and water basins.

Objectives for Kyrgyzstan: EXPECTED RESULTS AND ACHIEVEMENTS: Water managers in Central Asia and Afghanistan understand and apply sustainable IWRM on policy and applied levels. Networking, collaboration and trust among future water managers across Central Asia and Afghanistan have increased. National water ministries apply IWRM principles and provide improved support to Basin Management Organization. Basin planning principles in selected basins have improved.

description.narrative: The USAID Quality Health Care Project is a five-year program to improve the health status of Central Asians by incorporating modern quality improvement techniques and evidence-based international standards into ongoing reforms of health systems to assist Central Asian countries to improve their management, financing, and implementation of health services related to tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, maternal and child health services and cardiovascular disease.

title.narrative: Regional TB Program in Central Asia

description.narrative: This new Regional project will support the Government of Kyrgyz Republic's National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) in the implementation of its tuberculosis national strategic plan and will complement existing and planned projects. The project will build on efforts by other USAID projects and may provide technical assistance: 1) to ensure more equitable access to comprehensive and appropriate TB diagnostic and treatment services for vulnerable populations; 2) to improve laboratory services for providing more timely, quality TB and MDR-TB diagnosis; 3) to implement the patient centered outpatient treatment approach for TB and MDR-TB patients; 4) to improve enabling environment promoting TB services that meet international standards; 5) to strengthen human and institutional capacity of health system to manage TB and MDR-TB services; 6) to improve coordination and linkage of TB with other health sectors and CSOs; 7) to strengthen electronic TB MIS and using quality data by TB service providers and managers for evidence-based decision making at all levels.

(Kyrgyz Republic): .The objective of the regional Energy Links project is to increase national energy security for countries in Central Asia. By increasing transparent intra- and inter-regional energy trade, improving the legal and regulatory framework and investment climate for the countries' energy sectors, improving corporate governance, operations and commercialization of energy companies, and improving energy efficiency and demand-side management, the countries of Central Asia will increase the sustainability of their energy sectors and increase their ability to provide year-round, reliable power to their citizens. For the purposes of conducting regional activities under the project, the region is defined as Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, and Afghanistan and Pakistan. The bilateral Kyrgyz Republic activities focus on improving energy security and supporting energy-sector reform..

title.narrative: USAID Central Asia HIV Flagship Activity

description.narrative: The purpose of this HIV Regional Flagship Activity is to increase use of evidence-based government- and NGO-provided HIV prevention, treatment and care services by people living with HIV and key populations: people who inject drugs, prisoners, sex workers and men who have sex with men. By providing targeted technical assistance to the government and NGO sector to reach the populations driving the HIV epidemic, this Activity will ultimately contribute to reducing the number of new HIV infections and reducing HIV-related deaths in Central Asia.

Objectives for Central Asia, regional: EXPECTED IMPACT AND RESULTS..In the first year, 91 people living with HIV (PLHIV) started receiving antiretroviral therapy to improve quality of patient’s life and reduce HIV transmission. Community-based organizations supported by the project also support these people so that they adhere to their life-long treatment. In year two the project expects to cover over 1,700 people living with HIV..All people living with HIV reached by the project are screened for tuberculosis and escorted to treatment if necessary.The project has been developing, adapting and implementing innovative approaches such as rapid blood-based testing for HIV in high-risk groups like people who inject drugs and partners of PLHIV. The project trained five non-government organizations on case-detection and case-management approaches and community-based services for key populations. People living with HIV often come from closed social groups such as drug users that are very hard to reach for doctors or government. The project created a network of so called peer navigators, people coming from the same communities, to help PLHIV get treatment and care. The project continues to work with health providers and civil society organizations on reducing stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV. 120 medical health workers went through special training on these issues.

title.narrative: Dignity and Rights in Central Asia

description.narrative: Through the regional Dignity and Rights program, USAID will support activities with the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic and civil society partners that address Trafficking in Persons issues (across the spectrum of prevention, protection and policy reform) as well as activities in the trafficking in persons "nexus", such as migrants' rights and gender-based violence. Potential interventions include informational events, educational campaigns, and related media products supported by local civil society partners; protection services to support the return, rehabilitation, and reintegration of Victims of Trafficking (VOTs); improved general citizen awareness of rights-related issues, including trafficking; and improved mechanisms for cooperation between the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic, local society, and other regional actors.

Objectives for Asia (South & Central Asia): The project has three main objectives. This first is to increase public knowledge and support of human rights. The second is to equip the government and various non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to support survivors of human trafficking. The last one is to improve or update human rights laws with a focus on safe migration and human trafficking.

Objectives for Central Asia: REC facilitates trade among Central Asian countries, Afghanistan, as well as with other large trading partners. REC also works towards improving Central Asian countries’ pro-trade policies and procedures, increasing transport corridor performance, assisting Tajikistan in its WTO accession efforts, and strengthening the capacity of trade promotion agencies.

description.narrative: (Kyrgyz Republic): USAID/KR is in the final stages of completing its respective five-year strategic plan that will cover the period FY 2015 - FY 2019. USAID/KR requires support to help operationalize its strategy through a Mission-wide Performance Management Plan (PMP). Simultaneously, USAID/KR is launching a flagship four-year Economic Growth (KREG) project for which longer-term monitoring and evaluation support will be required.USAID Kyrgyz Republic expects that the Performance Management Plan (PMP) will serve as the primary programmatic framework and reference resource for the collection, compilation, analysis, verification and reporting of performance data on the implementation of USAID Kyrgyz Republic's FY 2015 - 2019 CDCS. In order to enhance uniformity in the usage, reporting and aggregation of data from all sources, the PMP shall provide explicit guidelines on the processes of data collection through to reporting, verification and validation.

description.narrative: FHI 360s Regional Partnership on Culture and Development (RPCD) program gathers and disseminates information to improve development efforts in the Middle East and North Africa region. The programs objectives include: 1) Conducting original and secondary research, evaluations and analysis for U.S. Agency for International Development missions in the Middle East and North Africa; 2) Building regional capacity by increasing the number of institutions and organizations that have access to development information; and 3) Sharing cutting-edge research and best practices in development across the region.In Egypt, the RPCD project conducts research in three focus areas: natural resource management, youth development and engagement, and democracy and governance.

title.narrative: Addressing Corruption Through Information and Organised Networking (ACTION)

description.narrative: To address governance and accountability in the MENA region, we are working towards three objectives: 1) Enhancing regional knowledge on access to information, through mapping and analysing the access-to-information environment; 2) Building the capacity of civil society, youth activists and selected media practitioners to strategically use the right to access public information in their demands for accountability and in anti-corruption advocacy; 3) Strengthening the links between civil society and youth activists on a regional level to increase their potential for activism and citizen engagement, through exploring the potential of social media.

title.narrative: OMEP: Powering Agriculture Hydroponic Green Farming Initiative

description.narrative: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)): The Powering Agriculture Initiative introduces an integrated model of hydroponic farming tied with renewable energy generation, demonstrating its applicability in Jordan on a large-scale commercial farm and on small-scale family farms. It builds local expertise and skills required for its wide-scale adoption, both in Jordan and the broader MENA region, developing profitable and sustainable business models that may be replicated and used to acquire lines of credit. In 2014, a feasibility study will be conducted to assess the economic feasibility of hydroponics in Jordan and the broader region. The project also supports commercial and household farmers in the construction and establishment of hydroponic systems, providing technical assistance and support. Educational materials will be shared with regional partners. These include (a) hydroponic system design; (b) system and management needs; (c) a replicable business model; and (d) analytical results of the performance and economics of hydroponics. FY2014 Benefitting~Countries include:~Jordan

title.narrative: OMEP: Modeling and Monitoring Agriculture & Water Resources Development

description.narrative: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)): Program funds will support the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture as a regional hub for generating and disseminating data. Through the development of regional networks, knowledge and data on cutting-edge concepts and modeling capabilities is transferred, thereby increasing scientific input into the policy process. FY 2014 resources will be used in two main areas: 1) to provide training to regional partners on climate change model downscaling, crop and irrigation mapping, and evapotranspiration and drought monitoring; 2) development of an information system platform, accessible through the internet, to be made available to governmental stakeholders, researchers and private groups and organizations, which will provide hydrologic data and model outputs for analysis and research; and 3) further development of the MENA-LIS (land information system) model for various scenarios of climate change in order to provide MENA water decision makers with new regional data that is essential to adaptation planning and policy development. FY2014 Benefitting~Countries include: Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco,~Tunisia, West Bank/Gaza

title.narrative: OMEP: Implementing International Standards for Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs)

description.narrative: (USAID Middle East Regional (MER)): USAID plans to use FY 2014 resources to support the introduction of international audit standards among several developing countries in the Middle East. Working through the International Organization for Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI) and its designated capacity building arm, the INTOSAI Development Initiative, USAID will be able to support the participation of Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia, and Yemen in this global initiative. The program will also draw on funding from Domestic Finance for Development (DF4D), a United States government policy initiative designed to elevate the importance of open government, fiscal transparency, and anti-corruption efforts in public finance. USAID's resources will be used to broaden stakeholder participation, transparency, and social accountability (e.g., public hearings, consultations, government disclosure), and to build capacity at INTOSAI's regional hub, ARABOSAI.FY2014 Benefitting Countries:~Algeria, Egypt,~Iraq, Jordan,~Libya, Morocco, Yemen

title.narrative: Enhance Climate Resiliency and Water Security in Maldives (Maldives GCC)

description.narrative: (Maldives): .The Enhance Climate Resiliency and Water Security in Maldives project will strengthen the knowledge and skills of water utility regulators, operators and island communities to make informed decisions on water resource management in the context of climate change adaptation...Given the limited freshwater resources in the Maldives, enhancing water security was identified as a key adaptation activity in Maldives' Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDCs) under UNFCC. FY 2016 funds will be used for the construction of a new integrated water resource management system mixing rain water and desalinated water providing safe and reliable supply for the 5,300 residents. The system will include a Reverse Osmosis Treatment Plant partially powered by solar energy, public rainwater harvesting units, a ground water recharge system and a water quality testing laboratory for islands in the region. .......

description.narrative: (Bangladesh): This activity will work to bolster economic growth in Bangladesh by creating greater efficiency in cross-border trade. It will provide technical assistance to the Government of Bangladesh (GOB) for the improvement of customs administration and the coordination of governance and interagency operations and policy. Assistance will include drafting regulations and procedures, training customs officials, convening stakeholder groups, and developing appropriate information technology platforms. The result will be improved access to trade-related information through an electronic web portal, and better customs clearance procedures and risk assessments, all of which will reduce the time and cost burden of importing or exporting goods. This activity will support trade across all sectors, but part of the activity will focus on the non-tariff barriers for the agriculture sector in cross-border trade with India.

title.narrative: Partnership for Environmental Law in China

description.narrative: The U.S.-China Partnership for Environmental Law works collaboratively with government institutions, non-government organizations, lawyers, judges, lawmakers and others to promote good environmental governance in China. As the most rapidly developing region on the planet, many countries in China are in urgent need of leaders to implement and enforce environmental laws and regulations, as well as policymakers and educators to develop the next generation of environmental advocates.

person-name.narrative: Zach Child, Regional Desk Officer, East Asia

description.narrative: The USAID-funded MTV EXIT (End Exploitation and Trafficking) is a global multimedia initiative produced by the MTV EXIT Foundation and supported regionally by USAIDs Regional Development Mission for Asia in Bangkok. The program provides awareness-raising activities for youth and vulnerable populations to prevent human trafficking. Public awareness activities are a key component of the broader effort to counter trafficking in persons in Asia, and are carried out with partner governments, local non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and civil society. This initiative operates throughout Asia with the support of USAID, the Australian Agency for International Development (AusAID), and the international NGO WalkFree. The $8 million public -private collaboration has leveraged $100 million in contributions from other donors. USAID and AusAID are together awarding a new four-year, Phase IV of the MTV EXIT Asia campaign to raise awareness and prevent human trafficking. This $11 million agreement will establish a partnership in which USAID will contribute approximately $5.5 million to AusAID for MTV EXIT. Secretary Clinton announced Phase IV during her visit to Australia in November 2012 for the annual Australia-U.S. Ministerial.

Objectives for Thailand: The U.S. Agency for International Development’s Community Partnership project aims to assist community-based organizations in Thailand to provide high quality HIV prevention, treatment and care to key populations, including men who have sex with men, transgender people, sex workers and people who inject drugs. To ensure high quality key population-led health services, this project will establish a training center for community-based organizations working with key populations to deliver efficient and effective HIV-related health services. In collaboration with local health authorities, this project will establish quality assurance systems in 13 priority provinces. It will also seek to mobilize financial resources and generate demand for sustaining this training program for key populations beyond the duration of the project.

title.narrative: Lower Emissions in Asia's Forests (LEAF) Program

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): Lowering Emissions in Asia's Forests aims to strengthen capacities of developing countries in Asia to produce meaningful and sustainable reductions in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the forestry-land use sector and to participate in and benefit from the emerging international Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and forest Degradation framework. Specific objectives include replicating and scaling up innovation through regional platforms and partnerships, supporting improved policy and market incentives for GHG reductions, demonstrating innovation in sustainable land management, and building capacities for economic valuation of forest ecosystem services and monitoring changes in forest carbon stocks. ~

title.narrative: Asia’s Regional Response to Endangered Species Trafficking (ARREST)

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): Asia's Regional Response to Endangered Species Trafficking (ARREST) combats the illegal trade in wildlife in Asia by 1) reducing consumer demand for illegally traded endangered species; 2) strengthening law enforcement capacity to deter the illicit trade; and 3) building regional learning networks and partnerships. The program enhances collaboration between the ASEAN Wildlife Enforcement Network (ASEAN-WEN) and new emerging networks, such as the South Asia Wildlife Enforcement Network and the Global Tiger Initiative (GTI), and strengthens ASEAN's collaboration with the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES), INTERPOL, and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. It also accesses the technical capabilities of interagency partners, including the U.S. Department of State International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Bureau, U.S.~Forest Service, U.S.~Fish and Wildlife Service, and the U.S.~Department of Justice. ARREST will operate in the ASEAN countries (except Singapore, Brunei, and Burma), as well as in China.

The Control and Prevention of Malaria (CAP-Malaria) project will advance the efforts of Cambodia's National Malaria Program to strengthen malaria prevention and control in the border areas of Cambodia where there is drug resistant malaria. The CAP-Malaria project will conduct behavior-change communication campaigns to increase awareness about malaria prevention, particularly among mobile and migrant workers. It will distribute approximately 50,000 insecticide-treated bed nets to vulnerable populations. CAP-Malaria will strengthen antenatal care practices among health workers in high prevalence areas to improve care for patients and the use of rapid diagnostic tests. The project will also track malaria-borne mosquitos and their biting behaviors and facilitate cross-border cooperation between Thai and Cambodian health authorities. This effort will reduce Cambodia's malaria burden, including malaria-related deaths, as well as move Cambodia towards the pre-elimination stage of malaria in specific areas.

title.narrative: Control and Prevention of Tuberculosis (CAP-TB) in the Mekong Region

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): .USAID RDMA's CAP-TB activity will continue to strengthen national and community-based efforts to combat multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) in the Mekong region. Using FY 2016 funds, the program will provide technical assistance to refine and implement comprehensive models for community-based interventions to better control the disease as well as to strengthen MDR-TB programs and services. The program's overall approach is founded upon patient-centered, community-driven implementation to enable faster diagnosis, higher treatment success rates, and more effective prevention of MDR-TB. In Thailand and China, RDMA will continue to strengthen the linkage between TB control systems and treatment facilities, as well as support the decentralization of TB expertise to provincial levels. .

title.narrative: Infectious Disease Emergence and Economics of Altered Landscapes (IDEEAL)

description.narrative: Land-use change is a significant driver of emerging infectious disease. Over 60 percent of emerging infectious diseases over the past six decades, including SARS, H1N1/Swine Flu, and HIV-AIDS have originated in animals, with nearly half of these linked to changes in land-use. Forest degradation resulting from agricultural intensification and other human activities accounts for about 15 percent of greenhouse gas emissions - roughly equivalent to the emissions generated by the entire global transportation sector. The key to reducing the threat from diseases with pandemic potential and slowing global climate change is to more accurately account for the value of ecosystems and base land-use choices on real benefits and costs.

description.narrative: (Thailand): USAID will provide a direct grant to support the operation of a non-profit management school in Thailand. The school will be an institution dedicated to building the quality of managers and management systems in non-profit organizations throughout Thailand and the region. Located at Khon Kaen University, courses provided will cover topics such as non-profit governance and leadership, finance and fundraising, decision-making, and the role of non-profit organizations in the 21st century. The activity will:?expand core curriculum and materials of Executive Training, undergraduate, and graduate courses;?design and formalize an undergraduate diploma certification course in Non-Profit Management, within the institution's existing Social Development program;?establish a one-stop shop where civil society organizations (CSOs) can access information on funding opportunities and the work of other CSOs, obtain legal advice, participate in digital literacy training, and seek advice from experts across a range of topics; ?organize roundtable discussions, seminars, and panel discussions; as well as?use new technologies or low-tech solutions to help CSOs connect and share experiences to better solve problems.

person-name.narrative: Zach Child, Regional Desk Officer, East Asia

description.narrative: With Sustainable Landscapes and Adaptation funding, RDMA will continue to support the establishment and implementation of a SERVIR hub in the Southeast Asia region. The SERVIR hub allows USAID to support the Southeast Asia region with remote sensing, geospatial information and decision support services for both climate change adaptation and land-based carbon sequestration. RDMA is a regional platform that can manage activities of the hub and outreach to bilateral USAID missions. The activity will benefit the Lower Mekong countries of Burma, Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam.

The activity focuses specifically on environmental conservation and addresses environmental challenges by building local capacity to assess potential natural resource management issues. Interventions will determine economically and environmentally viable land use options, and sustaining many natural resource-based livelihood options for the targeted Tibetan populations. This will include work in rangeland, watershed and livestock management including veterinary care, as well as the production of non-timber forest products and improved household energy efficiency to reduce deforestation. The activity's anticipated impacts include improved environmental resource management and use, thereby sustaining Tibetan traditional livelihoods and culture, focusing on income for Tibetans with a particular focus on women.

description.narrative: Develop and conduct needs assessments, baseline studies, targeted evaluations, special studies or other information-gathering efforts specifically for the design, monitoring and evaluation of USG-funded programs. This sub-element may also include developing and disseminating best practices and lessons learned, testing demonstration and/or pilot models, or the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks. Note: All such activities that are carried out by partners as an integral part of their monitoring and evaluation efforts for programs funded under other sub-elements should be included within those sub-elements.

(USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): Working across 11 Asian developing countries, the Low Emissions Asian Development program helps Asian governments, businesses, and institutions develop frameworks for sustained low-emission across all economic sectors. The activity complements the USG's global initiative for Enhancing Capacity for Low Emission Development Strategies (EC-LEDS). FY~2014 sustainable landscapes and clean energy funding will be used to develop and implement low emission development strategies (LEDS), build capacity on greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories and accounting, support carbon market development, and enhance regional capacity-building, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing platforms. The activity will enhance capacity in five countries to: prepare and complete high-quality national emissions inventories; develop, adopt, and use greenhouse gas accounting tools; establish new operational GHG trading platforms or registries; and adopt LEDS policies, plans, models and tools.

(Timor-Leste): The Health Improvement Project's (HIP) objective is to improve maternal, child, neonatal, and reproductive health outcomes in three districts. Through HIP, USAID will support the Ministry of Health (MOH) to implement evidence-based protocols in maternal and child health (MCH) and will increase community engagement in key MCH issues. HIP will improve the MOH's ability to collect and analyze data, leading to improved quality and efficiency of family planning services. Specific activities will include training for MOH staff, nurses and midwives, and support to improve health workers' counseling and clinical skills related to family planning. Partnerships with organizations such as St. John of God Health Care and the U.S. Navy Seabees will help USAID to maximize capacity-building efforts.

(Timor-Leste): O objectivo do Projecto de Melhoria da Saúde (HIP) é melhorar os resultados da saúde materna, infantil, neonatal e reprodutiva em três distritos. Através do HIP, a USAID apoiará o Ministério da Saúde (MS) na implementação de protocolos baseados em evidências na saúde materno-infantil (SMI) e aumentará o envolvimento da comunidade nas principais questões de SMI. A PGI melhorará a capacidade do Ministério da Saúde de recolher e analisar dados, conduzindo a uma melhor qualidade e eficiência dos serviços de planeamento familiar. As actividades específicas incluirão formação para funcionários do Ministério da Saúde, enfermeiros e parteiras, e apoio para melhorar o aconselhamento e as competências clínicas dos profissionais de saúde relacionadas com o planeamento familiar. Parcerias com organizações como a St. John of God Health Care e a U.S. Navy Seabees ajudarão a USAID a maximizar os esforços de capacitação.

title.narrative: Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Support Facility (ADAPT Asia-Pacific)

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): The Asia-Pacific Climate Change Adaptation Support Facility (ADAPT Asia-Pacific) responds to a key priority identified in RDMA's Asia-Pacific Regional Climate Change Adaptation Assessment (February 2010) and provides capacity building and governance support to increase access to funding for climate change adaptation projects. This program will: (i) strengthen human and institutional capacity to prepare high-quality climate change adaptation investment proposals; (ii) accelerate and ensure sustained access to financial resources for climate change adaptation investment projects; and (iii) support and strengthen a regional knowledge platform to share and replicate best practices. The program will also help develop specific curricula in regional institutions to address gaps in capacity identified by national governments and key stakeholders.

title.narrative: ASEAN-U.S. Partnership for Good Governance, Equitable and Sustainable Development and Security

description.narrative: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)-U.S. Partnership for Good Governance, Equitable and Sustainable Development and Security is a five-year project (2013-2018) supported by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and the United States Department of State to strengthen institutions and develop regional policies to advance ASEANs vision for political-security and social-cultural integration. The project supports ASEANs ability to advance good governance and political stability. For example, the project will help establish a judicial network to harmonize approaches on key issues in the rule of law in ASEAN. The project will also partner with the ASEAN Commission for the Promotion and Protection of the Rights of Women and Children to conduct activities to promote and strengthen these protections across the region.

description.narrative: Market forces and private sector investments, especially in agriculture, are driving forest loss in Southeast Asia. USAID Green Invest Asia aims to catalyze private finance into climate smart agriculture and sustainable business models to improve regional management of natural capital and promote sustainable growth. The activity will increase access to financing, introduce incentives, and support a wide range of business models that reduce emissions from improved land use practices. The activity will maintain U.S. leadership roles with regional financial institutions by connecting enterprises to those institutions that invest across companies, commodities, and countries. The activity will further increase opportunities for U.S. businesses seeking to invest in supply chains that originate in Asia, allowing them to access markets both inside and outside the region. The ratio of activity cost to leveraged investments over the five-year activity is estimated at 27:1.

Objectives for Asia (Far East Asia): Objective 1 - Identify Investments: To build a more robust pipeline of investment-worthy low emission AFOLU projects, USAID Green Invest Asia aims to 1) identify business models used across a range of companies seeking to “green” their supply chains; 2) provide services that enable businesses to adopt on-farm, climate-smart technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions; and 3) increase opportunities for sustainable companies to access finance. Objective 2 - FACILITATE Investments: In order to reduce the risk of “green” investments in the AFOLU sector, USAID Green Invest Asia draws on experts and industry networks to increase responsible investment. These actors build the knowledge and capacity of financial institutions to seek climate smart finance; to access customized financial services and products; and to adopt environment, social and governance standards. Objective 3 – Build a community of practice in sustainable landscape finance. USAID Green Invest Asia engages the full range of stakeholders in the financial, forestry and agricultural sectors. By working through existing networks, the activity will promote knowledge sharing and provide space for identifying business opportunities. Furthermore, the activity will foster cooperation among stakeholders to address systemic issues that hinder access to sustainable land use financing.

title.narrative: ASEAN-US Technical Assistance and Training Facility (TATF) Phase II

description.narrative: The ASEAN-US Technical Assistance and Training Facility provided comprehensive support for ASEAN integration through a collaborative, demand driven, and flexible assistance program. The Facility was housed in the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta, and funded by USAID and the U.S. Department of State under the ADThe project is involved in many activitiesVANCE program. The Facilitys strategy was aligned with ASEANs own Roadmap for an ASEAN Community that incorporates the blueprints for the political-security, economic, and socio-cultural communities. The Facility supported a wide variety of activities, including the ASEAN Regional Forum, the Human Rights Resource Center for ASEAN, the scorecard for the ASEAN Economic Community Blueprint, customs cooperation, a trade facilitation assessment, and a migrant worker law and regulation repository. The Facility also supported ASEAN in its response to Cyclone Nargis, delivered training in post-disaster damage assessment and needs analysis, and supported ASEANs pandemic preparedness and response program.

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): USAID support to IOM X inspires social resilience to human exploitation and trafficking in persons (TIP) in the Asia-Pacific Region, strengthening the adaptive capacity of potential young migrants. Support enables high-profile events, youth sessions, television programs (e.g., documentaries, drama, public service announcements, and music videos), as well as TIP-focused websites. The primary audience of USAID's IOM X Campaign is young people from 15 to 30 years of age, particularly those who are migrants or likely to become migrants. The secondary audience includes the general public in the ASEAN region. This activity builds greater levels of TIP knowledge among highly vulnerable groups, including young migrants and those that are likely to migrate. It also creates greater TIP awareness about human trafficking and how individuals can proactively respond to the issue among the general public, including host and origin communities.

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): RDMA will channel FY 2016 clean energy funding to the Asian Development Bank to implement the 2017 Asia Clean Energy Forum (ACEF), in Manila, the Philippines. With annual support from RDMA since 2007, ACEF has become the premier clean energy event for the Asia region, drawing over 1,500 participants from 60 countries across Asia and globally in 2015. ACEF provides a unique week-long venue for government officials, the private sector, technical experts, and civil society organizations to share the most innovative and important developments in clean energy in Asia and worldwide, and provides knowledge-sharing that directly complements and supports a range of USAID clean energy programs in the region. This activity supports countries' UNFCCC commitments to develop long-term national and subnational low emissions development strategies.

title.narrative: Asia Counter Trafficking In Persons (USAID Asia CTIP)

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): The USAID Asia Countering Trafficking In Persons (Asia CTIP) activity is part of a comprehensive U.S. government effort to address transnational and regional challenges to combat trafficking in persons. The activity has an overarching goal of facilitating an Asia region that more effectively addresses human trafficking risks and responses that transcend national borders through three priorities: 1) enhanced awareness and understanding regarding trafficking in persons and effective responses, 2) improved coordination and cooperation between source, transit and destination countries, and 3) engagement with the private sector to reduce trafficking in persons in targeted sectors. USAID Asia CTIP promotes free and open commerce within a rules-based environment that protects and promotes labor rights and advances the interests of U.S. companies. The activity also addresses exploitative practices that fund transnational criminal networks and destabilize the region..With FY 2022 funding, USAID Asia CTIP will focus on: 1) conducting needs assessments, studies, evaluations, and other information-gathering efforts to improve reporting and harmonization of CTIP monitoring and evaluation indicators across Asia, as well as building the capacity of academics, local research organizations, think tanks, and investigative journalists to produce high-quality regional analysis on trafficking in persons across the region; 2) increasing information sharing and harmonization of national trafficking definitions, laws, and penalties among the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states, and assisting member states in complying with their commitments under regional conventions and frameworks; and 3) collaborating with the private sector to reduce opportunities for trafficking in persons and forced labor in target sectors..

title.narrative: USAID Inform Asia Associate Award #2 - Technical assistance to strengthen malaria surveillance and the use of strategic information for malaria programming

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): USAID Inform Asia provides technical assistance to the national malaria program in Thailand to: 1) strengthen malaria surveillance systems for detection, notification, and response to all malaria cases; 2) evaluate malaria elimination approaches and strategies for implementation and scale-up; and 3) generate and use strategic information including routine data from anti-malarial drug therapeutic efficacy monitoring and documentation write-ups. Technical assistance will result in the development of key strategic information products, such as user-friendly informatics dashboards, technical assessments, advocacy briefs, and publications to inform relevant stakeholders and decision-makers. USAID expects that by the end of this award, Thailand's national malaria program will have increased technical capacity at national and subnational levels to use strategic information to plan, budget, implement, and monitor data-driven, technically sound, and cost-effective malaria programming that maximizes disease impact-a cornerstone in the road to a malaria-free Thailand by 2024. With FY 2022 funds, the activity will focus on providing monitoring and evaluation, data analysis for verification of subnational malaria elimination, prevention of re-introduction strategies that includes climate and environmental factors, and strengthening government staff capacity on data use and wider dissemination of lessons learned from Thailand's malaria elimination efforts. Achieving malaria elimination addresses global and U.S. national security priorities as it helps to create a more stable and prosperous region that advances American security and economic interests as well as enhancing regional prosperity and good governance. ...

A USAID/Filipinas fará parceria com a NOAA para melhorar a capacidade científica, técnica e de gestão do Governo das Filipinas para aumentar a resiliência ambiental e humana. A parceria centra-se na pesca sustentável, na gestão dos recifes de coral e na modelização das alterações climáticas/oceânicas para a pesca. *****(Indonésia): A USAID e a Administração Nacional Oceânica e Atmosférica dos EUA (NOAA) fazem parceria para fornecer assistência técnica e apoio à capacitação na gestão de recursos marinhos ao governo e ao povo da Indonésia. *****(Missão de Desenvolvimento Regional da USAID-Ásia (RDM/A)): Este Acordo Interagências (IAA) aproveitará a experiência científica e tecnológica da Administração Oceânica e Atmosférica Nacional (NOAA) para promover os objetivos da USAID na região, servindo como um mecanismo para missões em Ásia para projetar atividades estratégicas. As capacidades da NOAA na gestão dos recursos naturais, bem como na conservação dos oceanos e da pesca marinha contribuirão para cumprir os objectivos da USAID em matéria de biodiversidade, governação dos recursos naturais e segurança alimentar. Além disso, a RDMA trabalhará com a NOAA para desenvolver capacidades e fornecer assistência técnica que promova diretamente os objetivos de desenvolvimento da Agência relacionados com a conservação da biodiversidade, pesca sustentável e outros.*****(Timor-Leste): A atividade da Administração Oceânica e Atmosférica Nacional (NOAA) fornece assistência técnica ao Governo de Timor-Leste, ao Ministério da Agricultura e Pescas (MAF) e a outros profissionais marinhos parceiros. O apoio inclui uma série de atividades específicas destinadas a transformar a gestão dos recursos marinhos e costeiros na região a longo prazo. A NOAA estabelecerá várias ferramentas científicas fundamentais, fornecerá acesso a essas ferramentas de tomada de decisão e fornecerá assistência técnica ao GTL para ajudá-lo a compreender como utilizar as ferramentas para apoiar uma gestão sólida das pescas baseada no ecossistema. O objectivo desta actividade é ajudar o Governo de Timor-Leste.

USAID works with the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) to strengthen Indonesia's national parks and marine protected areas. USAID and DOI developed a partnership with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (MOEF) to strengthen national park management and biodiversity conservation at the national and park-specific levels through: 1) Training and Leadership Development for Improved Park Management; 2) Technical Assistance in National Park Resource Conservation and Management; and 3) Tourism and Visitor Services Development. USAID and DOI will build a cadre of effective leaders within the MOEF? and improve data collection, management, evidence-based planning and decision-making for wildlife protection through exchanges between national parks in the United States and Indonesia. Expected Results A cadre of effective leaders within MOEF;Improved decision making based on evidence;Strengthened national park management;Improved biodiversity conservation.*****(USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): This Interagency Agreement (IAA) will allow RDMA to leverage the expertise of multiple USDOI agencies to co-design integrated, strategic activities that build the capacity of, and train, regional institutions such as ASEAN, the Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Center, and the Coral Triangle Initiative. USDOI's technical capabilities will enable USAID to better (a) counter marine and terrestrial wildlife trafficking, (b) combat illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, (c) conserve marine biodiversity, and (d) improve fisheries management in Asia-Pacific region. As part of USAID RDMA's Smart Infrastructure for Mekong activity, USDOI's technical assistance will also mitigate potential negative social and environmental consequences from large infrastructure projects through peer review consultations on environmental and social impact assessments, hydrological modeling, climate change vulnerability, siting proposals, and technical training.

title.narrative: U.S.-APEC Technical Assistance to Advance Regional Integration (US-ATAARI)

description.narrative: The purpose of US-ATAARI is to help the APEC Secretariat and APEC member economies eligible for foreign assistance to advance economic integration and achieve the Bogor Goals of free and open trade and investment. The project has two components. Through Component 1, Nathan Associates is supporting APECs ongoing work in trade and investment liberalization, business facilitation, and economic and technical cooperation, as well as activities that accord with U.S. foreign policy priorities. Component 2 will build APEC's institutional capacity for strategic planning and support its work program. The project will produce policy studies, capacity assessments, training assessments, and advise APEC on integration, trade liberalization, and institutional management.

title.narrative: Lao PDR - U.S. International and ASEAN Integration II Project (LUNA II)

description.narrative: (Laos): As a landlocked country with a small consumer market, Laos must broaden and increase its trade and investment base to provide greater economic opportunities for its citizens. However, if Laos is to integrate into regional and global markets in a way that has broad economic benefits for its people, it will need assistance. LUNA II helps build the capacity of Government of Laos (GoL) officials to enact and implement critical economic reforms. LUNA II is assisting the GoL to build a database that will provide the basis for analyzing the costs and benefits of different negotiating positions given the needs of Lao businesses. LUNA II assistance helps the GoL to implement its international commitments to trade-related intellectual property rights, technical barriers to trade, trading rights, and legal transparency. By working on structural, regulatory, and policy-level challenges, USAID helps Laos raise incomes, create jobs, and permanently improve the living standards of the Lao people.

Objectives for Laos: In addition to the work on the electronic gazette, the project team will work with the Lao.government to help boost technical standards in trade such as strengthening the government agency.that certifies testing laboratories. USAID LUNA II also will provid assistance to launch and enhance the.official enquiry point for importers. This enquiry point helps traders understand technical regulations.required for importing goods to Lao PDR. With respect to the private sector, the activity will help Lao.exporters streamline procedures for issuing certificates of origin under an ASEAN Economic.Community pilot project and identified comparative advantages in various Lao products to assist Lao.trade negotiators.

title.narrative: Task Order #1 under the USAID Asia Learning and M&E Support Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract

description.narrative: (USAID Regional Development Mission-Asia (RDM/A)): The USAID Asia Learning and M&E Support contract provides: 1) a range of technical services to improve the M&E capacity of USAID missions, awardees and other stakeholders; 2) knowledge management and advisory services to inform decision-making and strengthen development programming; (3) capacity building for collaboration, learning and adapting within USAID missions; and (4) the technical and management capacity building of local and regional M&E partners..In addition to providing all requested services from USAID missions, this task order organizes a biennial M&E summit and maintains two rosters for USAID: one of M&E consultants, and another one of vetted Asian local and regional M&E organizations with the potential to provide services directly to USAID to increase the pool of M&E service providers in the region. The costs for this task order are shared between RDMA and bilateral missions that use its services..

Develop and conduct needs assessments, baseline studies, targeted evaluations, special studies or other information-gathering efforts specifically for the design, monitoring and evaluation of USG-funded programs. This sub-element may also include developing and disseminating best practices and lessons learned, testing demonstration and/or pilot models, or the preparation of strategic plans and other short-term programming tasks. Note: All such activities that are carried out by partners as an integral part of their monitoring and evaluation efforts for programs funded under other sub-elements should be included within those sub-elements.
The proposed work is covered by the existing CWT PAD and IEE and aligns with Task 1 Demand Reduction of Saving Species.

Objectives for Far East Asia, regional: This new activity supports efforts to strengthen law enforcement of wildlife crimes, reduce demand for illegally traded wildlife and foster international cooperation to combating wildlife crime. The activity builds on ASEAN member states’ commitment to introduce and enforce wildlife crime laws and promote international involvement in biodiversity conservation.

(Philippines): The Education Governance Effectiveness (EdGE) activity supports education decentralization and school-based management. EdGE provides mentoring for local chief executives, school division superintendents and supervisors, local school board members, and school heads on topics such as education planning, management, and evaluation. School governing councils are provided with training and mentors to develop and implement effective and responsive school improvement plans (SIPs). EdGE ties SIPs to local schoolboard budgets to reinforce the accountability of each governance structure in improving student achievement. With FY 2018 funds, EDGE will continue to leverage local government support and community participation to improve education outcomes with a special focus on improving reading skills and comprehension. Stakeholders will strengthen their planning and management and financing skills to more effectively utilize Special Education Funds. Through this partnership, USAID contributes to improved learning in the early grades by increasing government effectiveness, transparency, and accountability for education at the local level and increases the participation of stakeholders in education policy formulation and implementation.

(Filipinas): La actividad Eficacia de la Gobernanza Educativa (EdGE) apoya la descentralización de la educación y la gestión basada en las escuelas. EdGE brinda tutoría a directores ejecutivos locales, superintendentes y supervisores de divisiones escolares, miembros de juntas escolares locales y directores de escuelas sobre temas como planificación, gestión y evaluación de la educación. Los consejos de gobierno escolar reciben capacitación y mentores para desarrollar e implementar planes de mejora escolar (SIP) eficaces y receptivos. EdGE vincula los SIP con los presupuestos de las juntas escolares locales para reforzar la responsabilidad de cada estructura de gobierno en la mejora del rendimiento estudiantil. Con los fondos del año fiscal 2018, EDGE continuará aprovechando el apoyo del gobierno local y la participación de la comunidad para mejorar los resultados educativos con un enfoque especial en mejorar las habilidades de lectura y la comprensión. Las partes interesadas fortalecerán sus habilidades de planificación, gestión y financiación para utilizar de forma más eficaz los fondos de educación especial. A través de esta asociación, USAID contribuye a mejorar el aprendizaje en los primeros grados al aumentar la eficacia, la transparencia y la rendición de cuentas del gobierno para la educación a nivel local y aumenta la participación de las partes interesadas en la formulación e implementación de políticas educativas.

The Disaster Preparedness for Effective Response (PREPARE) project expedites emergency and reconstruction assistance in the event of disasters formally declared by the U.S. President in RMI. PREPARE will continue to support a functioning system that enables the rapid delivery of U.S. disaster response and reconstruction assistance in the country. The U.S. Government will support: 1) adult learning-based disaster preparedness training, mentoring, radio broadcasting and institutional strengthening; 2) warehousing capability to pre-position emergency equipment and commodities in strategic locations; 3) partnerships with strategic sectors that can provide assistance during times of emergencies for quick mobilization and distribution of emergency commodities and provision of technical assistance; and 4) increase technical knowledge of key stakeholders, such as NGOs, community organizations, volunteers, construction workers in the delivery of emergency and reconstruction assistance.*****(Micronesia): The Disaster Preparedness for Effective Response (PREPARE) activity expedites emergency and reconstruction assistance in the event of disasters formally declared by the U.S. President in the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM). PREPARE will continue to support a functioning system that enables the rapid delivery of U.S. disaster response and reconstruction assistance in the country. The U.S. Government will support: 1) adult learning-based curriculum and conduct trainings for disaster preparedness, radio broadcasting, mentoring, and institutional strengthening interventions; 2) warehousing capability to pre-position emergency equipment and commodities in strategic locations; 3) partnerships with strategic sectors that can provide assistance during times of emergencies; and 4) the increase technical knowledge of key stakeholders, such as NGOs, community organizations, volunteers, and construction workers in the delivery of emergency and reconstruction assistance.

description.narrative: (Philippines): The U.S. Government will invest $396,891 for the Coastal Community Adaptation Project (C-CAP) to build the resilience of coastal communities in the Pacific to withstand more intense and frequent weather events and ecosystem degradation in the short term (erosion, coral damage, flooding, drought, salt-water intrusion), and sea level rise in the long term by: (1) climate proofing small-scale community infrastructure such as coastal protection and rainwater catchment systems; and (2) building local capacity for disaster prevention and preparedness. Up to nine Pacific Island countries will benefit from C-CAP: Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

(Philippines): The Pacific-American Climate Fund supports grants to civil society organizations (CSOs) in Papua New Guinea (PNG) to improve biodiversity conservation and natural resource management. CSO grantees equip communities with awareness and skills, particularly women and youth, on sustainable environmental management practices and alternative livelihoods.The Pacific-American Climate Fund also builds the capacity of CSO grantees by guiding them through the grant cycle and helping them adopt sound project, financial management, and monitoring practices. This positions the CSOs on a path to self-reliance, enabling them to replicate their projects, collaborate with other organizations and engage in public-private partnerships. This is the last planned funding for the activity. To date, the implementing partner has strengthened the capacity of 28 CSOs across 10 countries in the Pacific, enabling the CSOs to implement grants that support locally driven and innovative initiatives in the forestry, fisheries, agriculture, and biodiversity conservation sectors...

title.narrative: Skills and Knowledge for Youth Employment (SKYE) Project

description.narrative: The Skills and Knowledge for Youth Employment (SKYE) project seeks to strengthen youths access to justice and equip youth with market-driven skills and attitudes to improve their ability to transition to the workforce. SKYE is targeting a total of 1,500 youth beneficiaries who are not yet equipped for integration into the workforce; many are school dropouts and/or involved in the juvenile justice system. SKYE also provides capacity building support to local partner organizations, relevant government ministries, and the court system.

description.narrative: (Brazil): USAID will work with the GOB's Agency for Cooperation (ABC) to leverage Brazilian expertise and funding to promote food security in Mozambique, Haiti, and Honduras. Assistance will promote small-scale horticulture production, nutrition education and outreach, and school feeding.In Mozambique we will introduce varieties of seeds adapted to local conditions, disseminate innovative post-harvest techniques, and assist the local government develop an advanced school feeding program that utilizes more nutritious foods and increases local food purchases. In Honduras, we will introduce renewable energy-based applications for cashew nut, sesame and honey value chains. In Haiti, we will support sharing of labs for tissue culture and micro propagation of roots and tubers with high nutritional value, and implement agricultural exchange programs. The activities in all three countries will address the basic determinants of food insecurity.

(Brasil): A USAID trabalhará com a Agência de Cooperação do Governo do Brasil (ABC) para aproveitar a experiência e o financiamento brasileiros para promover a segurança alimentar em Moçambique, Haiti e Honduras. A assistência promoverá a produção hortícola em pequena escala, a educação e sensibilização nutricional e a alimentação escolar. Em Moçambique, introduziremos variedades de sementes adaptadas às condições locais, disseminaremos técnicas inovadoras de pós-colheita e ajudaremos o governo local a desenvolver um programa avançado de alimentação escolar que utilize alimentos mais nutritivos e aumente as compras locais de alimentos. Nas Honduras, introduziremos aplicações baseadas em energias renováveis ​​nas cadeias de valor da castanha de caju, do gergelim e do mel. No Haiti, apoiaremos a partilha de laboratórios para cultura de tecidos e micropropagação de raízes e tubérculos com elevado valor nutricional e implementaremos programas de intercâmbio agrícola. As actividades nos três países abordarão os determinantes básicos da insegurança alimentar.

title.narrative: Proyecto de Competitividad Económica de USAID

description.narrative: (El Salvador): Seventy-five percent of illegal migrants to the United States report economic reasons for emigrating. El Salvador's economy has been stagnant, averaging two percent GDP growth over the last 15 years. The COVID-19 pandemic has made the situation worse by contracting the economy and putting jobs at risk. This activity creates livelihoods and deters illegal migration by assisting the government and private sector institutions to increase micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises' (MSMEs) productivity and competitiveness in key economic sectors that are most likely to employ those with the most limited economic opportunities and likely to attempt to illegally migrate.The activity will assist El Salvador's economic recovery from COVID-19. FY 2020 funding will provide technical assistance to public and private business development service providers, help MSMEs increase exports and sales, increase business productivity, enhance women's participation in business, and improve government service delivery to MSMEs.Further, the activity will promote and facilitate high-quality U.S. investment opportunities to counter the potential investments of malign actors. It will assess the feasibility and risk of proposed Chinese investments while promoting and raising awareness of U.S. and other foreign direct investments. The activity will conduct an assessment of industries where this is most viable and provide technical assistance to our partners to realize those opportunities. The activity will stimulate private sector investments in support of America Crece by supporting the Development Finance Corporation's (DFC) pipeline of bankable deals and investment opportunities.... .... ..

(El Salvador): Setenta y cinco por ciento de los inmigrantes ilegales a Estados Unidos informan razones económicas para emigrar. La economía de El Salvador ha estado estancada, con un crecimiento promedio del PIB del dos por ciento en los últimos 15 años. La pandemia de COVID-19 ha empeorado la situación al contraer la economía y poner en riesgo los empleos. Esta actividad crea medios de vida y disuade la migración ilegal al ayudar al gobierno y a las instituciones del sector privado a aumentar la productividad y la competitividad de las micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MIPYMES) en sectores económicos clave que tienen más probabilidades de emplear a personas con las oportunidades económicas más limitadas y que probablemente intenten migrar ilegalmente. La actividad ayudará a la recuperación económica de El Salvador del COVID-19. La financiación del año fiscal 2020 brindará asistencia técnica a proveedores de servicios de desarrollo empresarial públicos y privados, ayudará a las MIPYMES a aumentar las exportaciones y las ventas, aumentará la productividad empresarial, mejorará la participación de las mujeres en los negocios y mejorará la prestación de servicios gubernamentales a las MIPYMES. Además, la actividad promoverá y facilitará oportunidades de inversión estadounidenses de alta calidad para contrarrestar las posibles inversiones de actores malignos. Evaluará la viabilidad y el riesgo de las inversiones chinas propuestas y al mismo tiempo promoverá y creará conciencia sobre las inversiones directas estadounidenses y extranjeras. La actividad llevará a cabo una evaluación de las industrias donde esto es más viable y brindará asistencia técnica a nuestros socios para aprovechar esas oportunidades. La actividad estimulará las inversiones del sector privado en apoyo de América Crece mediante el apoyo a la cartera de acuerdos financiables y oportunidades de inversión de la Corporación Financiera de Desarrollo (DFC).... .... ..

Funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and best known simply as Alianzas (which means alliance), the project pioneered new mechanisms for cooperation between public and private partners. Alianzas formed alliances by inviting new potential partners to participate in existing projects and jointly create solutions that could be implemented through nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) or government-led projects. The overall purpose of Alianzas was to extend coverage and improve the quality of existing health and education services and incorporate state-of-the-art and proven approaches for increased social sector investments. Improving Access to and Use of Quality Health Care and Nutrition Services, Alianzas focused on maternal and child health, including promoting breastfeeding and family planning, as well as community and school nutrition, and workplace programming in support of HIV prevention.

Financiado por la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional (USAID) y mejor conocido simplemente como Alianzas (que significa alianza), el proyecto fue pionero en nuevos mecanismos de cooperación entre socios públicos y privados. Alianzas formó alianzas invitando a nuevos socios potenciales a participar en proyectos existentes y crear conjuntamente soluciones que podrían implementarse a través de organizaciones no gubernamentales (ONG) o proyectos liderados por gobiernos. El propósito general de Alianzas era ampliar la cobertura y mejorar la calidad de los servicios de salud y educación existentes e incorporar enfoques probados y de última generación para aumentar las inversiones en el sector social. Para mejorar el acceso y el uso de servicios de atención médica y nutrición de calidad, Alianzas se centró en la salud materna e infantil, incluida la promoción de la lactancia materna y la planificación familiar, así como la nutrición comunitaria y escolar, y la programación en el lugar de trabajo en apoyo de la prevención del VIH.
