title.narrative: Second Generation Alliances for Social Investment
Alianzas de Segunda Generación para la Inversión Social
Alianzas de Segunda Generación para la Inversión Social

description.narrative: The second generation of Alianzas builds on the original programs goals, utilizing alliances to improve education and health. Since 2005, the partnership has had several key achievements through the formation of 104 individual private sector alliances: providing more than 100,000 scholarships, delivering over 150,000 textbooks, installation of 80 computer labs, training approximately 7,500 teachers, and training more than 5,000 health providers. In addition, more than 350,000 people received reproductive health and family planning informational messages, 26,000 mothers and 22,000 children took part in a maternal/child health program, over 46,000 people gained access to safe water after Tropical Storm Stan, and 7.4 million Guatemalans received vaccines to eradicate measles and rubella.

La segunda generación de Alianzas se basa en los objetivos del programa original y utiliza alianzas para mejorar la educación y la salud. Desde 2005, la asociación ha logrado varios logros clave a través de la formación de 104 alianzas individuales con el sector privado: otorgando más de 100.000 becas, entregando más de 150.000 libros de texto, instalación de 80 laboratorios de computación, capacitación de aproximadamente 7.500 maestros y capacitación de más de 5.000 proveedores de servicios de salud. Además, más de 350.000 personas recibieron mensajes informativos sobre salud reproductiva y planificación familiar, 26.000 madres y 22.000 niños participaron en un programa de salud maternoinfantil, más de 46.000 personas obtuvieron acceso a agua potable después de la tormenta tropical Stan y 7,4 millones de guatemaltecos recibieron vacunas para erradicar el sarampión y la rubéola.

description.narrative: (Haiti): With FY 2021 funds, USAID will continue to build the capacity of the Ministry of Health (MOH) to take ownership of Haiti's comprehensive health information system, French abbreviation SISNU. The program supports the MOH to strengthen SISNU by integrating health records across digital and paper-based reporting platforms, addressing information and technical gaps, improving data quality, and promoting better system governance and stewardship. Through these continuous improvements, SISNU will provide data needed by the MOH for better public health decision-making, helping the Government of Haiti provide higher quality maternal and child health care and treatment plus family family planning to the Haitian people. In FY 2022, USAID will continue improving the quality of data recorded by SISNU and will support the expansion of the health information system to capture and analyze data recorded by community health workers (CHWs) in the District Health Information System (DHIS2) community health tracking module...USAID will continue to support the Carte Sanitaire (CS), a web-based geographic information system that complements the SISNU system by providing key information on health institutions like the global positioning system (GPS) location, contact information and the availability and type of health services provided at each facility. The MOH intends to use the tool to identify and respond to emerging public health issues before they become a crisis...

Increase the availability and use of proven life-saving interventions that address the major killers of mothers and children and improve their health and nutrition status, including effective maternity care and management of obstetric complications; prevention services including newborn care, routine immunization, polio eradication, safe water and hygiene, and micronutrients; improved maternal, infant and young child feeding; and treatment of life-threatening childhood illnesses.

Supports the following illustrative program-funded costs: salaries of US, FSN, and TCN and other staff such as PSCs, RSSAs, PASAs, CASUs working for the US Government managing, administering, and supporting programs and their program-funded benefits such as housing, travel, transportation, education allowances etc; institutional contractors that provide such staff, rent, IT services, the program-funded share of utilities, staff training costs and the cost of developing and administering training programs, equipment and supplies, ICASS, vehicle fuel and maintenance, maintenance contracts, janitorial services, operational unit web page development and maintenance, outreach such as publications and the cost of their preparation (including staff costs), and technical assistance to ensure USG compliance with regulations.

title.narrative: Preventing Transmission of HIV/AIDS from High Risk Groups in Nicaragua
Prevenir la transmisión del VIH/SIDA entre grupos de alto riesgo en Nicaragua
Prevenir la transmisión del VIH/SIDA entre grupos de alto riesgo en Nicaragua

description.narrative: The purpose of the Program will be to support the country efforts to slow the spread of HIV/AIDS in Nicaragua among most at risk populations (MARPS) to the broader population. Most at risk populations include men who have sex with men (MSM) and female sex workers (FSW), among others.

El propósito del Programa será apoyar los esfuerzos del país para frenar la propagación del VIH/SIDA en Nicaragua entre las poblaciones de mayor riesgo (MARPS) a la población en general. Las poblaciones de mayor riesgo incluyen hombres que tienen sexo con hombres (HSH) y trabajadoras sexuales (TSF), entre otros.

El propósito del Programa será apoyar los esfuerzos del país para frenar la propagación del VIH/SIDA en Nicaragua entre las poblaciones de mayor riesgo (MARPS) a la población en general. The Peru Alternative DevelopmentProgram combinedtraditional assistance activities agricultural technologytransfer, business development,microfinance, behavior changecommunications, civil societystrengthening, natural resourcemanagement, and local governance with voluntary eradication.In an environment that hastraditionally opposed the presenceof certain government agencies,or where government is largelyabsent, PDA concentrated itssupport on clients who chose toabandon illegal behavior.

El Programa de Desarrollo Alternativo del Perú combinó actividades tradicionales de asistencia, transferencia de tecnología agrícola, desarrollo empresarial, microfinanzas, comunicaciones para el cambio de comportamiento, fortalecimiento de la sociedad civil, gestión de recursos naturales y gobernanza local con erradicación voluntaria. En un entorno que tradicionalmente se ha opuesto a la presencia de ciertas agencias gubernamentales, o donde el gobierno está en gran medida ausente, PDA concentró su apoyo en clientes que optaron por abandonar el comportamiento ilegal.

title.narrative: PTPA Forest Governance and Environmental Implementation
Gobernanza forestal e implementación ambiental de la PTPA

description.narrative: (Peru): We will invest $1,660,000 of FY 2014 GCC-Sustainable Landscapes and $99,000 of Biodiversity funding to provide technical assistance to both national and regional-level Government of Peru entities in order to strengthen the institutional framework for forest management. Work will help the Peruvian Forest Service, Regional Environmental Authorities, and the Forest Supervision Agency to build capacity for forest management and implement a national forest information system to track the origin of wood products. We will help entrepreneurs and native communities improve production processes and sustainable management of forest resources. We will support public consultations on the regulations for the Forestry and Wildlife Law that will have emissions' benefits through the promotion of conservation, protection, and sustainable forest management. Efforts will advance Enhancing Capacity for Low Emission Development Strategies (EC-LEDS) in Peru. (IM 40086 - $1,660,000 direct GCC-SL)

(Perú): Invertiremos $1,660,000 de Paisajes Sostenibles del CCG para el año fiscal 2014 y $99,000 de fondos de Biodiversidad para brindar asistencia técnica a entidades del Gobierno de Perú a nivel nacional y regional con el fin de fortalecer el marco institucional para el manejo forestal. El trabajo ayudará al Servicio Forestal del Perú, las Autoridades Ambientales Regionales y la Agencia de Supervisión Forestal a desarrollar capacidades para el manejo forestal e implementar un sistema nacional de información forestal para rastrear el origen de los productos de madera. Ayudaremos a empresarios y comunidades nativas a mejorar los procesos productivos y el manejo sustentable de los recursos forestales. Apoyaremos las consultas públicas sobre el reglamento de la Ley Forestal y de Vida Silvestre que tendrá beneficios en emisiones a través de la promoción de la conservación, protección y manejo forestal sostenible. Los esfuerzos impulsarán el Mejoramiento de la Capacidad para Estrategias de Desarrollo Bajas en Emisiones (EC-LEDS) en Perú. (IM 40086 - $1.660.000 directo GCC-SL)

(Peru): We will invest $2.7 million of FY 2014 GCC-Sustainable Landscapes funds in the Peru Forest Sector Initiative (PFSI), a bilateral program which is part of the regional Amazon Forest Sector Initiative (AFSI). In Peru, PFSI promotes compliance with the U.S.-Peru Trade Promotion Agreement, including its Forest Governance Annex, and contributes to the implementation of the USG's Enhancing Capacity for Low Emission Development Strategies Memorandum of Understanding with Peru by increasing access to natural resources management information, ensuring the implementation of a timber tracking system, and supporting the legal and regulatory framework for sustainable forest concession management. PFSI also builds technical capacity of the Amazonian Regional Governments as well as the newly formed Peruvian Forest Service. It works with national and regional governments, indigenous organizations, and non-governmental organizations throughout the region. (IM 42809 - $2,700,000 direct GCC-SL)

(Perú): Invertiremos $2,7 millones de fondos de Paisajes Sostenibles del CCG para el año fiscal 2014 en la Iniciativa del Sector Forestal del Perú (PFSI), un programa bilateral que forma parte de la Iniciativa del Sector Forestal Amazónico regional (AFSI). En Perú, PFSI promueve el cumplimiento del Acuerdo de Promoción Comercial entre Estados Unidos y Perú, incluido su Anexo de Gobernanza Forestal, y contribuye a la implementación del Memorando de Entendimiento para el Mejoramiento de la Capacidad para Estrategias de Desarrollo Bajas en Emisiones del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos con Perú al aumentar el acceso a la información sobre el manejo de recursos naturales, garantizar la implementación de un sistema de seguimiento de la madera y apoyar el marco legal y regulatorio para el manejo sostenible de las concesiones forestales. El PFSI también fortalece la capacidad técnica de los gobiernos regionales amazónicos, así como del recién formado Servicio Forestal Peruano. Trabaja con gobiernos nacionales y regionales, organizaciones indígenas y organizaciones no gubernamentales de toda la región. (IM 42809 - $2.700.000 directo GCC-SL)

(Perú): Invertiremos $2,7 millones de fondos de Paisajes Sostenibles del CCG para el año fiscal 2014 en la Iniciativa del Sector Forestal del Perú (PFSI), un programa bilateral que forma parte de la Iniciativa del Sector Forestal Amazónico regional (AFSI). En Perú, PFSI promueve el cumplimiento del Acuerdo de Promoción Comercial entre Estados Unidos y Perú, incluido su Anexo de Gobernanza Forestal, y contribuye a la implementación del Memorando de Entendimiento para el Mejoramiento de la Capacidad para Estrategias de Desarrollo Bajas en Emisiones del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos con Perú al aumentar el acceso a la información sobre el manejo de recursos naturales, garantizar la implementación de un sistema de seguimiento de la madera y apoyar el marco legal y regulatorio para el manejo sostenible de las concesiones forestales. El PFSI también fortalece la capacidad técnica de los gobiernos regionales amazónicos, así como del recién formado Servicio Forestal Peruano. Trabaja con gobiernos nacionales y regionales, organizaciones indígenas y organizaciones no gubernamentales de toda la región. (IM 42809 - $2.700.000 directo GCC-SL)

(Peru): Investiremos US$ 2,7 milhões dos fundos do GCC-Paisagens Sustentáveis ​​do ano fiscal de 2014 na Iniciativa do Setor Florestal do Peru (PFSI), um programa bilateral que faz parte da Iniciativa Regional do Setor Florestal da Amazônia (AFSI). No Peru, a PFSI promove o cumprimento do Acordo de Promoção Comercial EUA-Peru, incluindo o seu Anexo de Governança Florestal, e contribui para a implementação do Memorando de Entendimento do Governo dos EUA para Estratégias de Desenvolvimento de Baixas Emissões com o Peru, aumentando o acesso a informações de gestão de recursos naturais, garantindo a implementação de um sistema de rastreamento de madeira e apoiando o quadro jurídico e regulamentar para a gestão sustentável de concessões florestais. O PFSI também fortalece a capacidade técnica dos Governos Regionais da Amazônia, bem como do recém-formado Serviço Florestal Peruano. Trabalha com governos nacionais e regionais, organizações indígenas e organizações não governamentais em toda a região. (IM 42809 - US$ 2.700.000 direto GCC-SL)

title.narrative: Peru and Andean Trade Capacity Building (PATCB) Program
Programa Perú y Fortalecimiento de Capacidades Comerciales Andinas (PATCB)
Programa Perú y Fortalecimiento de Capacidades Comerciales Andinas (PATCB)

description.narrative: The primary goal of the program is to support successful implementation of the U.S.-Peru Trade Promotion Agreement (USPTA), which entered into force in February 2009. Open and prosperous trade via that and other agreements, such as APEC and a proposed Trans Pacific Partnership, will broaden economic growth and reduce poverty. To help ensure this, the PATCB program will endow Peru with 1) A fully functional management information system, management procedures,and judicial protocols to enforce labor rights; 2) Training programs in intellectual property rights for the customs administration and the judiciary; 3) Municipalities with simplified procedures for business registration; and 4) Faster clearance times for goods in port.

El objetivo principal del programa es apoyar la implementación exitosa del Acuerdo de Promoción Comercial Perú-Estados Unidos (USPTA), que entró en vigor en febrero de 2009. El comercio abierto y próspero a través de ese y otros acuerdos, como APEC y una propuesta Asociación Transpacífico, ampliará el crecimiento económico y reducirá la pobreza. Para ayudar a garantizar esto, el programa PATCB dotará al Perú de 1) un sistema de información de gestión, procedimientos de gestión y protocolos judiciales totalmente funcionales para hacer cumplir los derechos laborales; 2) Programas de capacitación en derechos de propiedad intelectual para la administración aduanera y el poder judicial; 3) Municipios con procedimientos simplificados para el registro de empresas; y 4) Tiempos de despacho de mercancías más rápidos en puerto.

title.narrative: Environment Peace Initiative for Colombia (EPIC)-Fondo Patrimonio Natural (FPN)
Iniciativa de Paz Ambiental para Colombia (EPIC)-Fondo Patrimonio Natural (FPN)

description.narrative: (Colombia): .USAID/Colombia's Conservation and Governance activity conserves the Andean Amazon ecosystem and fosters sustainable rural development by providing technical assistance to farmers to develop land management best practices, and improve productivity of combined woodland/grazing and agroforestry systems. In order to protect forest remnants, the activity supports farmers to establish nature reserves on their own land, which are key elements in conservation corridors to enhance biological connectivity. The activity also supports farmers in strengthening the cheese value chain, from production to marketing, and in securing long-term commercial agreements, as well as eco-tourism by supporting a "cheese trail" which stops at various farms and reserves allowing tourists to learn about both the cheese-making process and conservation of the Amazon ecosystem. This tourism component helps to achieve our conservation goals in Colombia through conservation agreements signed with local farmers that protect existing forests and watersheds as private natural reserves, rehabilitate degraded land and establish agroforestry systems. The program is promoting ecotourism linked to these conservation efforts and culture of the cattle ranching, branded as 'The Cheese Route'. This activity is implemented through a local organization, and directly contributes to the USG Mission Objective to improve conditions for inclusive rural economic growth and sustainable development. FY 2018 funding will provide $330,541 for the FY 2018 SFOAA-legislated Andean Amazon Biodiversity directive... .. .

(Colombia): La actividad de Conservación y Gobernanza de USAID/Colombia conserva el ecosistema andino amazónico y fomenta el desarrollo rural sostenible brindando asistencia técnica a los agricultores para desarrollar mejores prácticas de manejo de la tierra y mejorar la productividad de los sistemas combinados de bosques/pastoreo y agroforestales. Para proteger los remanentes de bosques, la actividad apoya a los agricultores para que establezcan reservas naturales en sus propias tierras, que son elementos clave en los corredores de conservación para mejorar la conectividad biológica. La actividad también apoya a los agricultores en el fortalecimiento de la cadena de valor del queso, desde la producción hasta la comercialización, y en la obtención de acuerdos comerciales a largo plazo, así como el ecoturismo mediante el apoyo a una "ruta del queso" que se detiene en varias granjas y reservas que permiten a los turistas aprender tanto sobre el proceso de elaboración del queso como sobre la conservación del ecosistema amazónico. Este componente turístico ayuda a lograr nuestros objetivos de conservación en Colombia a través de acuerdos de conservación firmados con agricultores locales que protegen los bosques y cuencas existentes como reservas naturales privadas, rehabilitan tierras degradadas y establecen sistemas agroforestales. El programa promueve el ecoturismo vinculado a estos esfuerzos de conservación y cultura de la ganadería, denominado 'La Ruta del Queso'. Esta actividad se implementa a través de una organización local y contribuye directamente al objetivo de la misión del Gobierno de los Estados Unidos de mejorar las condiciones para el crecimiento económico rural inclusivo y el desarrollo sostenible. El financiamiento del año fiscal 2018 proporcionará $330,541 para la directiva de biodiversidad de la Amazonía Andina del año fiscal 2018, legislada por la SFOAA... .. .

title.narrative: Environment Peace Initiative for Colombia-(EPIC) Fondo Acción Ambiental y Niñez -(FAAN)
Iniciativa de Paz Ambiental para Colombia-(EPIC) Fondo Acción Ambiental y Niñez -(FAAN)

description.narrative: (Colombia): .This Program is part of USAID's efforts to conserve the Andean Amazon ecosystem, focusing on the most threatened region of the Colombian Amazon where the agricultural frontier and deforestation are rapidly expanding. The program works in conservation corridors, establishing sustainable productive systems and connecting products to markets as an economic incentive to set aside and/or restore forest fragments. It also provides capacity-building, policy-development and decision-making tools for local governments to scale up and sustain these efforts. The program is also serving as a bridging mechanism between two larger Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) programs in the Pacific region. The program strengthens community governance and livelihood activities to implement eight REDD+projects, involving 19 Afro-Colombian and indigenous communities and protecting over 800,000 hectares of forest in one the world's most important biodiversity hotspots..

(Colombia): Este Programa es parte de los esfuerzos de USAID para conservar el ecosistema amazónico andino, enfocándose en la región más amenazada de la Amazonía colombiana donde la frontera agrícola y la deforestación se están expandiendo rápidamente. El programa trabaja en corredores de conservación, estableciendo sistemas productivos sostenibles y conectando productos a mercados como incentivo económico para apartar y/o restaurar fragmentos de bosque. También proporciona herramientas de creación de capacidad, desarrollo de políticas y toma de decisiones para que los gobiernos locales incrementen y sostengan estos esfuerzos. El programa también sirve como mecanismo puente entre dos programas más grandes de Reducción de Emisiones por Deforestación y Degradación Forestal (REDD+) en la región del Pacífico. El programa fortalece la gobernanza comunitaria y las actividades de medios de vida para implementar ocho proyectos REDD+, que involucran a 19 comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas y protegen más de 800.000 hectáreas de bosque en uno de los puntos críticos de biodiversidad más importantes del mundo.

(Jamaica): $2,000,000 will be directly attributed to the development of a new clean energy activity. To achieve its objectives, the program will work with multiple stakeholders: national policy makers and planners, utilities, project developers, financial institutions, and end-users. Specifically, USAID/Jamaica's Clean Energy program will establish pre-conditions for clean energy development (policies and planning), optimizing variable renewable integration and reducing losses in the electricity sector, and accelerating private sector clean energy investment. USAID/Jamaica will use a mix of on-the-ground results and higher level enabling environment reform. A breakdown of the clean energy funding by sub-pillar will be determined once the program design is complete (end FY 2015), but will likely focus on renewables, energy efficiency, enabling environment, and LEDS planning/development. Information from the ongoing Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) support from State Department will feed into Clean Energy activities in the new procurement.

description.narrative: (State Western Hemisphere Regional): .Quality crime data and analysis is outdated in most Caribbean countries, limiting resources for effective decision-making on a comprehensive approach to youth crime and violence prevention. If Caribbean national authorities have access to standardized and disaggregated crime data reporting, it will improve the enabling environment for effective youth crime and violence prevention with reliable and comparable data for citizen security policy and decision making. Building on milestones achieved under the activity thus far, USAID will continue to support improved data-driven decision-making by strengthening the capacity of criminal justice agencies to better collect, analyze, and target crime administrative data. This support includes national survey data to inform policies that aim to address the root causes of crime and violence. Additionally, USAID will support the procurement and establishment of crime information management systems to equip law enforcement with the tools to accomplish these goals. These efforts will align crime and violence reporting indicators in the region to international standards, pilot a digitized police crime incident reporting system that transitions police from a paper-based to digitized recording crime system; and produce national surveys on gender-based violence and crime victimization... .

description.narrative: University of the West Indies-Cave Hill School of Business/Indiana University: Barbados: Supporting Entrepreneurs through the JOBS Initiative - The partnership between Cave Hill School of Business (CHSB) in Barbados and Indiana UniversitysKelley School of Business focuses on supporting the growth of an entrepreneurial culture and diversifying the service-oriented economies in Barbados and the Organization of Eastern Caribbean Countries (OECS) region. The partnership seeks to create new business opportunities and to foster entrepreneurship, especially among young adults. The partnership is working toward two main objectives: Strengthen Cave Hills institutional capacity by improving its facultys ability to teach studentsand advise emerging entrepreneurs on critical components of entrepreneurial and enterprise development and by developing and enhancing degree programs, course curriculum and applied research techniques on entrepreneurship; and Enhance the outreach capacity of Cave Hill to offer quality entrepreneurship training and services to foster entrepreneurship across the OECS; as well as youth program initiatives to more effectively engage young adults in entrepreneurship practice.

Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: CBSI-ESC-ESF-Community, Family, and Youth Resilience (CFYR) Program

description.narrative: (State Western Hemisphere Regional): The Eastern and Southern Caribbean (ESC) has suffered from growing levels of youth crime and violence, with five countries ranking in the top-twenty worldwide for the number of homicides per capita. Youth crime and violence prevention will improve by reducing risk factors and increasing resilience factors strengthened within targeted communities where high rates of crime and violence occur. USAID's community-level violence prevention activity will continue to focus resources on three countries with among the highesT crime and violence problems (St. Lucia, St. Kitts and Nevis, and Guyana) and further concentrate programming in five crime hot-spot communities within each of these three countries. The program seeks to reduce risk factors and increase resilience factors for youth aged 10 to 29 through interventions with families, communities, non-government entities, service providers, and government agencies. By training youth and community workers (eg. social workers and probation officers) to understand and address violence in their communities, the program promotes ownership and oversight. The activity also addresses the needs of youth at an individual level, providing vocational and life skills training through after-school and summer camp programming, as well as counseling and psycho-social services for youth who have exhibited risk factors that make them most vulnerable to violence. USAID will continue to use data to match at-risk youth with interventions, including work opportunities, and help community stakeholders identify and implement solutions to create an environment for positive youth development. The project will continue its efforts to systematically advance sustainability by building local capacity to manage the counseling and workforce development programs after USAID funding ends. At the end of the project, key tools, methodologies and approaches will be transferred to targeted government and local partner

Entre las actividades ilustrativas se incluyen las siguientes: reforma del sector público y gestión pública; planificación estratégica, formulación de políticas y presupuestos; desarrollar la capacidad ministerial; desarrollo de capacidades civiles y cívicas; supervisión formal (legislativa, fiscal, derechos humanos); y supervisión informal (grupos de vigilancia de la sociedad civil).

title.narrative: Regional Trade and Market Alliances Project
Proyecto de Alianzas Regionales de Comercio y Mercado

description.narrative: (USAID Central America Regional): .The purpose of the Regional Trade and Market Alliances activity is to foster inclusive economic growth in Central America by improving the business enabling environment for intraregional trade and exports. The principal aim is to consolidate selected agriculture value chains in the region and improve access to export markets by building alliances between key public and private organizations, supporting trade facilitation measures, harmonizing trade regulations, and improving the institutional capacity of various players in the private sector. ..FY 2016 funded activities will promote public-private dialogue in trade facilitation to accelerate the region's economic integration, assist in streamlining border management processes, and support the Central American Secretariat for Economic Integration to improve its internal systems, and modernize information management platforms. .

(USAID Regional Centroamérica): .El propósito de la actividad Alianzas Regionales de Comercio y Mercado es fomentar el crecimiento económico inclusivo en Centroamérica mejorando el entorno empresarial propicio para el comercio y las exportaciones intrarregionales. El objetivo principal es consolidar cadenas de valor agrícolas seleccionadas en la región y mejorar el acceso a los mercados de exportación mediante la creación de alianzas entre organizaciones públicas y privadas clave, el apoyo a medidas de facilitación del comercio, la armonización de las regulaciones comerciales y la mejora de la capacidad institucional de varios actores del sector privado. ...Las actividades financiadas durante el año fiscal 2016 promoverán el diálogo público-privado en materia de facilitación del comercio para acelerar la integración económica de la región, ayudar a agilizar los procesos de gestión fronteriza y apoyar a la Secretaría Centroamericana de Integración Económica para mejorar sus sistemas internos y modernizar las plataformas de gestión de información. .

title.narrative: USAID/Guatemala-Strengthening the Quality of Care and Improving the Quality of Life for People Living with HIV and other Vulnerable Populations Program
USAID/Guatemala-Programa Fortalecimiento de la Calidad de Atención y Mejoramiento de la Calidad de Vida de Personas que Viven con VIH y Otras Poblaciones Vulnerables
USAID/Guatemala-Programa Fortalecimiento de la Calidad de Atención y Mejoramiento de la Calidad de Vida de Personas que Viven con VIH y Otras Poblaciones Vulnerables

description.narrative: (Guatemala): With FY 2014 funds, USAID will continue providing technical assistance to strengthen the capacity of Ministry of Health (MOH) staff to use the Human Resources Information System (iHRIS), one of the tools the MOH uses for human resources management actions and workforce policy decisions. iHRIS has proved its value by helping the MOH to uncover several false positions in the payroll; thus, it has become a tool to fight corruption and improve transparency in the MOH. Additionally, the use of iHRIS reduces information processing time. As a result of USAID's FY 2014 assistance, iHRIS will be connected to other Government of Guatemala data sets and will become an integral element of the MOH information system. Recent changes in the structure and functioning of the MOH require additional support to technical cadres and stakeholders to advocate for and increase active participation in the use of the iHRIS.

(Guatemala): Con fondos del año fiscal 2014, USAID continuará brindando asistencia técnica para fortalecer la capacidad del personal del Ministerio de Salud (MS) para utilizar el Sistema de Información de Recursos Humanos (iHRIS), una de las herramientas que utiliza el Ministerio de Salud para las acciones de gestión de recursos humanos y las decisiones de política laboral. iHRIS ha demostrado su valor al ayudar al Ministerio de Salud a descubrir varias posiciones falsas en la nómina; por lo tanto, se ha convertido en una herramienta para combatir la corrupción y mejorar la transparencia en el Ministerio de Salud. Además, el uso de iHRIS reduce el tiempo de procesamiento de la información. Como resultado de la asistencia de USAID para el año fiscal 2014, iHRIS se conectará a otros conjuntos de datos del Gobierno de Guatemala y se convertirá en un elemento integral del sistema de información del Ministerio de Salud. Los cambios recientes en la estructura y funcionamiento del Ministerio de Salud requieren apoyo adicional a los cuadros técnicos y a las partes interesadas para defender e incrementar la participación activa en el uso del iHRIS.

PAPA con el Servicio Forestal de EE. UU. - Promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y la integración comercial mediante el desarrollo de capacidades sanitarias y fitosanitarias (SPS) y otras actividades relacionadas con la agricultura

PAPA con el Servicio Forestal de EE. UU. - Promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y la integración comercial mediante el desarrollo de capacidades sanitarias y fitosanitarias (SPS) y otras actividades relacionadas con la agricultura

PAPA con el Servicio Forestal de EE. UU. - Promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y la integración comercial mediante el desarrollo de capacidades sanitarias y fitosanitarias (SPS) y otras actividades relacionadas con la agricultura

description.narrative: This mechanism aims to enhance food security and promote regional agricultural trade in Central America and the Dominican Republic. It will help: 1) build public and private sector SPS capacity; 2) improve access to markets; 3) improve food security statistical systems; and 4) enhance laboratories' capabilities to diagnose chemical and biological pathogens and residues. The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will assist the Ministry of Agriculture to implement an effective public-private SPS inspection system. Training will be provided to producers to increase compliance with international SPS standards, and to assist them in exporting agricultural products to the U.S. Technical assistance and training will also be provided to small-scale farmers for the implementation of the Food Safety Modernization Act. The mechanism will support trilateral cooperation between the U.S., Chile and Guatemala to transfer knowledge from the Chilean experience to Guatemala.

Este mecanismo tiene como objetivo mejorar la seguridad alimentaria y promover el comercio agrícola regional en Centroamérica y República Dominicana. Ayudará a: 1) desarrollar la capacidad sanitaria y fitosanitaria de los sectores público y privado; 2) mejorar el acceso a los mercados; 3) mejorar los sistemas estadísticos de seguridad alimentaria; y 4) mejorar las capacidades de los laboratorios para diagnosticar patógenos y residuos químicos y biológicos. El Departamento de Agricultura de los Estados Unidos (USDA) ayudará al Ministerio de Agricultura a implementar un sistema público-privado de inspección MSF eficaz. Se brindará capacitación a los productores para aumentar el cumplimiento de las normas sanitarias y fitosanitarias internacionales y ayudarlos a exportar productos agrícolas a los EE. UU. También se brindará asistencia técnica y capacitación a los pequeños agricultores para la implementación de la Ley de Modernización de la Inocuidad de los Alimentos. El mecanismo apoyará la cooperación trilateral entre Estados Unidos, Chile y Guatemala para transferir conocimientos de la experiencia chilena a Guatemala.

El mecanismo apoyará la cooperación trilateral entre Estados Unidos, Chile y Guatemala para transferir conocimientos de la experiencia chilena a Guatemala.

(USAID Central America Regional): The Trilateral Cooperation activity will primarily assist USAID Missions and governments of the Northern Triangle countries (El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras) to build trilateral cooperation among the United States, Central American countries, and selected donor countries, primarily from Latin America, as relevant. USAID will support the transfer of technical expertise, technology and knowledge, training and other resources to implement short-term, exploratory or pilot programs that address specific needs of Central American countries to support the U.S. Strategy for Engagement in Central America. Some interventions USAID is planning to carry out under this mechanism are in the areas of trade facilitation, supporting regional systems integration and coordination in border procedures; and clean energy that will advise municipal level leadership in the region on adopting successful models of off-grid energy financing to increase lighting in high crime areas.

(USAID Regional América Central): La actividad de Cooperación Trilateral ayudará principalmente a las Misiones de USAID y a los gobiernos de los países del Triángulo Norte (El Salvador, Guatemala y Honduras) a construir una cooperación trilateral entre los Estados Unidos, los países centroamericanos y los países donantes seleccionados, principalmente de América Latina, según corresponda. USAID apoyará la transferencia de experiencia técnica, tecnología y conocimiento, capacitación y otros recursos para implementar programas piloto o exploratorios de corto plazo que aborden necesidades específicas de los países centroamericanos para apoyar la Estrategia de Estados Unidos para la Participación en Centroamérica. Algunas intervenciones que USAID planea realizar bajo este mecanismo son en las áreas de facilitación del comercio, apoyo a la integración de sistemas regionales y coordinación en procedimientos fronterizos; y energía limpia que asesorará a los líderes municipales de la región sobre la adopción de modelos exitosos de financiamiento de energía fuera de la red para aumentar la iluminación en áreas de alta criminalidad.

description.narrative: Vanderbilt University conducts AmericasBarometer democracy, governance and citizen security surveys in Latin America and Caribbean countries and related country and regional analyses. Country reports and, when requested, oversampling reports can be prepared that compare results from areas with USAID-programs to the rest of the country. The biennial survey includes 40,000 survey across 25 countries in the hemisphere. Vanderbilt is also conducting an impact evaluation of the Agencys crime prevention activities under the Central America Regional Security Initiative (CARSI) in Guatemala, El Salvador and Panama.

La Universidad de Vanderbilt lleva a cabo encuestas de democracia, gobernanza y seguridad ciudadana del Barómetro de las Américas en países de América Latina y el Caribe y análisis nacionales y regionales relacionados. Se pueden preparar informes de país y, cuando se soliciten, informes de sobremuestreo que comparen los resultados de áreas con programas de USAID con el resto del país. La encuesta bienal incluye 40.000 encuestas en 25 países del hemisferio. Vanderbilt también está realizando una evaluación de impacto de las actividades de prevención del delito de la Agencia en el marco de la Iniciativa de Seguridad Regional de Centroamérica (CARSI) en Guatemala, El Salvador y Panamá.

description.narrative: (USAID Central Africa Regional): Illicit trade in wildlife undermines biodiversity and security in Central Africa, where well-armed, well-organized networks of criminals exploit porous borders and weak institutions to profit from trading in poached wildlife. There is also widespread evidence that groups who trade in wildlife products also trade in other illicit products such as precious minerals and arms and may also engage in human trafficking. USAID's Protected Garamba-Chinko Protected Area Program will directly support the management of the Garamba National Park in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Chinko Nature Reserve in the Central African Republic (CAR). This activity leverages substantial private financial and technical resources from outside the country and builds the capacity of local parks management agencies in both countries at the local and national level. FY 2022 Biodiversity funding will be used to strengthen wildlife law enforcement and security by supporting park rangers, developing protected area management capacity, and engaging within the surrounding community to provide incentives and increase support for conservation. The vehicle for this assistance will be technical assistance, training, procurement of materials and support of outreach work to the protected area management structures in Garamba National Park and Chinko Nature Reserve....This activity will contribute to maintaining the ecological integrity of the humid forest ecosystem of the Congo Basin, which is vital to regional stability and a U.S. foreign policy priority. It contributes to the Joint Strategic Plan Strategic Objective 2.2: (Promote healthy, educated and productive populations in partner countries to drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives) by protecting natural resources critical to long term, sustainable growth, and food and water security....... .

(Central African Republic): The CONNECT activity aims to connect citizens to the post electoral political process in CAR and refugee areas, advocating for equal rights and protections for religious and ethnic minotiry populations. In order to achieve this objective, Internews works directly with local partners: Reseau des Journalistes pour les Droits de l'Homme (RJDH), Coalition des Femmes pour la Paix et la Reconciliation (CFPRCA) and various CAR media outlets. .The work of Internews and partners involves: (i) ensuring improved quality information to the CAR population by providing training, coaching and mentoring to Central African journalists; (ii) providing technical and editorial assistance to Central African media outlets with a specific focus on promoting coverage for women journalists and gender issues; (iii) establishing a media resource center (MRC) offering an internet connection, radio studio, and laptops for journalists' use, providing them with tools to perform, research, and improve production in a professional way ; (iv) providing information to CAR refugees in IDP camps, and (v) providing technical and advocacy support to the Haut Conseil de la Communication (HCC)..

title.narrative: Support for Scaling up Mobile Money in Malawi

description.narrative: (Malawi): USAID/Malawi's Mobile Money activity supports the expansion of low-cost mobile banking and electronic funds transfer (EFT) services. It increases financial inclusion, broadens access to financial services, and delivers affordable financial services to the poor. FY 2014 activities include:-Integrate mobile money into on-going USAID activities. -Develop scale by supporting government EFT initiatives and donor and nongovernmental organizations' cash transfer programs. -Support the delivery of electronic vouchers for 60,000 smallholder farmers participating in Malawi's Farm Input Subsidy Program.Activities will result in increased access to financial services by underserved communities, especially poor households, smallholder farmers, and micro and small enterprises, and build demand for other high-value wireless communication applications.

title.narrative: DGC- Aga Khan Foundation GDA - Yetu Initiative

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Yetu initiative will build on the achievements of the first two phases, to support Local Development Organizations (LDOs) in Kenya through the Kaunti Kuimarisha Uendelevu - Strengthening County Sustainability - Annual Program Statement (APS). Yetu will engage country-wide LDOs to foster community-led, community-managed, and community-owned development, a main principle of J2SR. Yetu will also build LDOs' capacity in community philanthropy to leverage assets, abilities, and trust in addressing local development. This will catalyze the sustainability of local civil society..Yetu will support successful APS applicants to engage county stakeholders in the co-creation and formation of LDOs. Once registered, Yetu will support the LDOs to design strategic plans that incorporate county priorities, context and systems findings. The initiative will support LDO members through a blend of courses, networking opportunities, and in-person mentorship. Consequently, this will strengthen the community of practice. Through Yetu's support, LDOs will work with county authorities to influence local development priorities based on members' and citizen's needs. The activity will also support LDOs to lead in priority setting, outreach to vulnerable and marginalized populations, and partner with county governments and the private sector to coordinate COVID-19 responses. It will also mobilize local resources to address the pandemic and its secondary effects. The Interventions will engage county governments, private sector, and civil society to support LDOs to be resilient and citizen-responsive to drive inclusive growth, all critical to Kenya's journey to self-reliance. Importantly, Yetu initiative supports Kenya's Joint Strategic Plan by ensuring stability and building citizen-responsive local governance that will help transform lives, communities, and economies in Kenya.

description.narrative: Under this Participating Agency Service Agreement (PASA), the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and its associated U.S. Land Grant University partners will provide long- and short-term personnel and targeted technical assistance to USAID/Kenya in support of its activities under the Feed the Future and Power Africa initiatives, as well as other economic growth programs. The PASA will support the Office of Economic growth in strategy development, program design, analysis, and management of its resilience programming, specifically to address agriculture and food security, business development, climate change, as well as energy programs. (Nigeria): -The Nigeria Expanded Trade and Transportation (NEXTT) activity is a response to trade and transportation-related barriers undermining Nigeria's food production and making the country largely dependent on food imports.-The NEXTT activity will support the Government of Nigeria (GON) to improve trade policy, build trade capacity, and remove bottlenecks impeding the free flow of goods, particularly agricultural goods along the Lagos-Kano-Jibiya (LAKAJI) Corridor. NEXTT in FY 2014 will streamline these interventions to better match the Feed the Future value chains and the GON Agricultural Transformation Agenda in specific Staple Crop Processing Zones located along the corridor. -The activity will facilitate new agricultural investments along the LAKAJI Corridor through a Project Development Facility and strengthen the relationship between private sector business and exporting enterprises.

description.narrative: (USAID Democracy, Conflict and Humanitarian Assistance (DCHA)): The Continuing Appropriations Resolution Act, 2014 provided USAID/DCHA/PPM $20 million in New Obligation Authority (NOA) for the Complex Crises Fund (CCF). As noted in previous years, CCF is a contingency fund and information will be entered retroactively consistent with the procedures established by State/F. CCF enables the U.S. Government to respond quickly during critical windows of opportunity by providing resources to address unforeseen political, social, or economic challenges that threaten stability, and support sustainable programs to foster long-term development. The goal is to seize opportunities to advance peaceful transitions, democratic governance, and development progress. The CCF-funded "Transition Initiatives for Stabilization" (TIS) is USAID's bridge between medium to longer-term development programs that require the initial conditions for improved stability to have been established in order to take root.~~Community-driven, quick-impact programs in targeted areas increase economic opportunities in the short term, build confidence in local and federal administrations, and contribute to more comprehensive recovery. With this award, activities have been expanded into new communities recently liberated from the al-Shabaab terrorist organization during recent offensives by the African Union Mission to Somalia (AMISOM).

title.narrative: REI- East Africa Trade and Investment Hub

description.narrative: (USAID East Africa Regional): The USAID East Africa Trade and Investment Hub (the Hub) partners, with East African and U.S. businesses, attract investment that transforms the East African private sector into a vibrant global trading partner. The Hub promotes a more predictable, transparent, and enabling business environment in East Africa by supporting adherence to intra-regional and international trade agreements, and conformity to international standards. The Hub leads in providing technical support to regional governments and private sector firms, and advancing U.S. interests under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). The purpose of the activity is to improve the region's trade competitiveness, encourage the diversification of exports beyond natural resources, and promote broader, more-inclusive economic growth for a more food secure and resilient East Africa. USAID will use FY 2018 resources to build on prior investments to: partner with East African and U.S. businesses in attracting investment that transforms the East African private sector into vibrant global trading partners; promoting a more predictable, transparent, and enabling business environment in East Africa by supporting adherence to intra-regional and international trade agreements and conformity to international standards; improving the region's trade competitiveness; encouraging the diversification of exports beyond natural resources; and promoting broader, more-inclusive economic growth leading to a more food secure and resilient East Africa. A specific focus will be to expand trade and investment linkages between the United States and East African countries by providing greater targeted support to U.S. firms and continued firm-level support to East African companies to meet U.S. standards and buyer requirements for exports under AGOA. These efforts support the U.S. administration priorities by opening new markets and commercial opportunities for U.S. businesses...

description.narrative: Access to inputs such as improved seed varieties, fertilizer and crop protection products are imperative to the transformation of the agricultural sector. The project sought to modernize seed distribution systems, facilitate smallholder farmer access to improved seed varieties, improve seed production technologies, and strengthen links to credit and markets. Specifically, The Seeds Project strengthened West Africas seed system across Burkina Faso, Ghana, Mali, Niger, and Senegal.

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): Peace through Development II (PDevII) is USAID/West Africa's flagship regional peace and governance program in support of the Trans-Sahara Counter Terrorism Partnership (TSCTP). USAID designed PDevII as a development response to counter the appeal of extremist movements in specific country contexts, with a particular focus on at-risk youth. It targets specific regions in the focus countries for TSCTP, which include Niger, Chad and Burkina Faso. TSCTP efforts are informed by a series of joint assessments and ongoing planning with interagency partners.PDev II builds on lessons learned from the previous regional program and earlier pilot programs. The overall goal of the program is to increase resistance to violent extremism in at-risk communities by empowering youth, increasing moderate voices, enhancing civil society capacity to address community issues, and strengthening local governance.Violent extremist groups in the region [including Al Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM) and Boko Haram] attempt to use both weak governance and extremist messaging to radicalize more moderate communities with the aim of increasing numbers as well as expanding their support base. Using improved governance and media, the program fosters an environment that makes it more difficult for terrorists to gain local sponsorship, sanctuary and support. Program activities increase involvement of targeted populations in public life as well as improve access to messages of tolerance and peace, directly addressing critical issues such as weak governance and extremist messaging. USAID also works with youth associations, community organizations, and local governments to develop supportive roles and models to promote youth as community leaders, communicators and outreach coordinators to help spread tolerance and peace information and more participatory processes at the local level.By the end of the PDev II program, USAID expects the following results: (1) youth e

L'USAID a conçu le PDevII comme une réponse de développement visant à contrer l'attrait des mouvements extrémistes dans des contextes nationaux spécifiques, avec un accent particulier sur les jeunes à risque. Il cible des régions spécifiques dans les pays cibles du TSCTP, notamment le Niger, le Tchad et le Burkina Faso. Les efforts du TSCTP s'appuient sur une série d'évaluations conjointes et de planification continue avec des partenaires interinstitutionnels. L’objectif global du programme est d’accroître la résistance à l’extrémisme violent dans les communautés à risque en responsabilisant les jeunes, en augmentant les voix modérées, en renforçant la capacité de la société civile à résoudre les problèmes communautaires et en renforçant la gouvernance locale. Les groupes extrémistes violents de la région [dont Al-Qaïda au Maghreb islamique (AQMI) et Boko Haram] tentent d’utiliser à la fois une gouvernance faible et des messages extrémistes pour radicaliser des communautés plus modérées dans le but d’augmenter leur nombre et d’élargir leur base de soutien. Grâce à une gouvernance et à des médias améliorés, le programme favorise un environnement qui rend plus difficile aux terroristes d'obtenir un parrainage, un refuge et un soutien locaux. Les activités du programme augmentent la participation des populations ciblées à la vie publique et améliorent l'accès aux messages de tolérance et de paix, en abordant directement des problèmes critiques tels que la faible gouvernance et les messages extrémistes. (Burkina Faso) : . .Pour faire avancer l'Initiative présidentielle contre le paludisme, l'USAID continuera à soutenir le plan stratégique 2016-2020 du Programme national de lutte contre le paludisme (NMCP) à travers l'activité d'amélioration des soins contre le paludisme (IMC) en accomplissant les tâches suivantes : ..Améliorer la prévention du paludisme à l'appui de la stratégie nationale de lutte contre le paludisme ; améliorer les interventions de diagnostic et de traitement du paludisme à l'appui de la stratégie nationale de lutte contre le paludisme ; etAméliorer la capacité technique du PNLP à planifier, concevoir, gérer et coordonner un programme complet de lutte contre le paludisme. L'USAID travaillera dans les 70 districts sanitaires du pays. L'activité sera centrée sur les interventions clés suivantes : ..1) traitement préventif intermittent pour les femmes enceintes ; .2) prise en charge des cas de paludisme simple et grave à l'aide de tests de diagnostic rapide, de thérapies combinées à base d'artémisinine et de médicaments recommandés pour le paludisme grave ; .3) chimioprévention du paludisme saisonnier chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans ; .4) amélioration de la qualité de la gestion des cas de paludisme grâce à la formation et à la supervision des agents de santé communautaires et des établissements de santé ; .5) L'IMC se concentrera sur le renforcement des capacités du PNLP et assurera sa durabilité. ..IMC est avant tout un projet de prestation de services de renforcement des systèmes de santé avec des fonds pour financer des services, y compris, mais sans s'y limiter : la formation préalable et continue des prestataires de soins de santé, la mise en œuvre d'interventions de lutte contre le paludisme telles que la distribution de médicaments pendant la SMC et le soutien aux groupes de travail techniques du comité directeur du PNLP... Les interventions ci-dessus soutiennent l'objectif 3 de la mission : Promouvoir des opportunités économiques et un développement social équitables, sous-objectif 3.2.2 : Élargir les interventions de prévention et de contrôle du paludisme pour réduire le nombre de décès liés au paludisme et sous-objectif 3.2.4 : Contribuer à l'effort national visant à mettre fin aux décès évitables d'enfants et de mères..

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): With FY 2018 funds, USAID will pilot and scale up market-based household solutions to meet sanitation needs in Cote d'Ivoire, Benin and Ghana. .FY 2018 activities will include:.Marketing and sales of branded latrine products;.Increasing access to finance for households and landlords to reduce the most stubborn barriers to the access of latrines and improved sanitation; .Rolling out vacuum truck call centers to make it easier and cheaper to desludge a septic tank; and.Communicating and disseminating successes and challenges in market-based sanitation. .Having developed and tested toilet products and desludging services in urban Cote d'Ivoire, Benin and Ghana, USAID will scale up the marketing and sales of individual household latrines, public latrines and desludging services. In a sector that is heavily influenced by local government, the program works closely with building code enforcement to improve the enabling environment for installing latrines in every household. This will strengthen local businesses in the sanitation sector and address the public health issues associated with open defecation and poorly managed sanitation in urban areas. Addressing urban sanitation needs reduces morbidity, leading to healthier, more productive citizens..This activity asserts U.S. leadership and influence, and fosters opportunities for U.S. economic interests through its partnership with American companies. It directly contributes to JSP Goal 2 (Renew America's Competitive Advantage for Sustained Economic Growth and Job Creation) by promoting American business interests to improve sanitation in West Africa. USAID pilots the use of a low cost latrine platform developed by American Standard, a Japanese company, based in New Jersey. .

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): Large Scale Food Fortification (LSFF) offers an evidence-based and cost-effective way to provide essential vitamins and minerals lacking in diets, particularly among the most vulnerable, when implemented under appropriate conditions. Several development programs have shown that if (i) the food vehicle is widely and regularly consumed by the target population, (ii) the food vehicle is industrially processed, and (iii) LSFF programming is well designed and implemented, results from this effort are transformational. Moreover, the LSFF approach is a more efficient way of delivering key micronutrition to beneficiaries because it does not require behavioral change from the target population...Illustrative activities for FY 2023 funds will include:.Supporting safe, nutritious food processing aligned with international standards and Hazard Assessment and Critical Control Point practices;.Working with West African Health Organization (WAHO) and other organizations to improve knowledge and information exchange on nutrition surveillance and best practices sharing;.Partnering with food manufacturers to increase food fortification, and explore fortification opportunities with food products for vulnerable populations in the region; and.Policy analysis and advocacy by the private sector for an improved business enabling environment...In the long term, this activity will advance U.S. economic interests by implementing nutrition sensitive agriculture policies that build partner countries' capacity to address food and nutrition security while creating opportunities for U.S. prosperity. It contributes to the National Security Strategy by supporting Program Element EG.3.3: Nutrition sensitive agriculture of the U.S. Global Food Security Strategy...Geographic Focus: All 15 ECOWAS countries with specific attention to the six GFSS targeted countries : Ghana, Liberia, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, and Senegal..

(USAID Région Afrique de l'Ouest) : Avec les fonds de l'exercice 2018, l'USAID pilotera et étendra des solutions domestiques basées sur le marché pour répondre aux besoins d'assainissement en Côte d'Ivoire, au Bénin et au Ghana. .Les activités de l'exercice 2018 comprendront :.La commercialisation et la vente de produits de latrines de marque ;.L'amélioration de l'accès au financement pour les ménages et les propriétaires afin de réduire les obstacles les plus tenaces à l'accès aux latrines et à un assainissement amélioré ; .Déployer des centres d'appels de camions aspirateurs pour rendre plus facile et moins coûteuse la vidange d'une fosse septique ; et.Communiquer et diffuser les réussites et les défis en matière d'assainissement basé sur le marché. Après avoir développé et testé des produits de toilettes et des services de vidange dans les zones urbaines de Côte d'Ivoire, du Bénin et du Ghana, l'USAID intensifiera la commercialisation et la vente de latrines familiales individuelles, de latrines publiques et de services de vidange. Dans un secteur fortement influencé par le gouvernement local, le programme travaille en étroite collaboration avec l'application du code du bâtiment pour améliorer l'environnement propice à l'installation de latrines dans chaque foyer. Cela renforcera les entreprises locales du secteur de l’assainissement et résoudra les problèmes de santé publique associés à la défécation à l’air libre et à un assainissement mal géré dans les zones urbaines. Répondre aux besoins d’assainissement urbain réduit la morbidité, ce qui conduit à des citoyens plus sains et plus productifs. Cette activité affirme le leadership et l’influence des États-Unis et favorise les opportunités pour les intérêts économiques américains grâce à son partenariat avec des entreprises américaines. Il contribue directement à l'objectif 2 du JSP (Renew America's Competitive Advantage for Sustained Economic Growth and Job Creation) en promouvant les intérêts des entreprises américaines pour améliorer l'assainissement en Afrique de l'Ouest. L'USAID teste l'utilisation d'une plateforme de latrines à faible coût développée par American Standard, une société japonaise basée dans le New Jersey. .

(USAID Région Afrique de l'Ouest) : L'enrichissement alimentaire à grande échelle (LSFF) offre un moyen fondé sur des données probantes et rentable de fournir des vitamines et des minéraux essentiels manquant dans l'alimentation, en particulier chez les plus vulnérables, lorsqu'il est mis en œuvre dans des conditions appropriées. Plusieurs programmes de développement ont montré que si (i) le véhicule alimentaire est largement et régulièrement consommé par la population cible, (ii) le véhicule alimentaire est transformé industriellement et (iii) la programmation LSFF est bien conçue et mise en œuvre, les résultats de cet effort sont transformationnels. De plus, l'approche LSFF est un moyen plus efficace de fournir une micronutrition clé aux bénéficiaires car elle ne nécessite pas de changement de comportement de la part de la population cible... Les activités illustratives pour les fonds de l'exercice 2023 comprendront : Soutenir une transformation alimentaire sûre et nutritive alignée sur les normes internationales et les pratiques d'évaluation des risques et de maîtrise des points critiques ; des opportunités d'enrichissement en produits alimentaires pour les populations vulnérables de la région ; et.Analyse des politiques et plaidoyer du secteur privé en faveur d'un meilleur environnement propice aux affaires... À long terme, cette activité fera progresser les intérêts économiques des États-Unis en mettant en œuvre des politiques agricoles sensibles à la nutrition qui renforcent la capacité des pays partenaires à assurer la sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle tout en créant des opportunités pour la prospérité des États-Unis. Il contribue à la stratégie de sécurité nationale en soutenant l'élément de programme EG.3.3 : Agriculture sensible à la nutrition de la stratégie américaine de sécurité alimentaire mondiale... Concentration géographique : les 15 pays de la CEDEAO avec une attention particulière aux six pays ciblés par le GFSS : Ghana, Libéria, Mali, Niger, Nigeria et Sénégal..

Délégitimer le recours à la terreur en cherchant à mettre en évidence l'immoralité fondamentale, les coûts et les impacts négatifs du recours à la violence et à souligner les avantages du recours à des alternatives pacifiques et tolérantes.

(USAID West Africa Regional): USAID will support media development, strategic communications, and attitudinal change activities as part of USAID's broader countering violent extremism (CVE) effort in the Sahel. FY 2019 activities will include:Broadcasting radio soap operas and interactive shows in multiple local languages, reaching an estimated daily audience of 3 million listeners.Expanding the reach and strengthening the capacity of 80 local community radio station partners through technical training, management training, and equipment support.Using community groups, social media platforms, and innovative technologies to engage audience members and CVE actors in positive messages. . ..A randomized control trial demonstrated that listening to a USAID-funded serialized radio drama on CVE led to a significant (18%) increase in likelihood to list collaboration with security forces as a key strategy to combat violent extremism. Through this and other activities, Voices for Peace (V4P) advances countries on their journey to self-reliance by increasing the commitment of communities to CVE, and increasing the capacity of governments and civil society actors to work within communities, thereby addressing the grievances typically leveraged by violent extremism organizations (VEOs). V4P currently works across the Sahel and targets regions with VEO presence..V4P defends U.S. national security interests by preventing the spread of violent extremist groups that seek to harm Americans at home and abroad. This activity contributes directly to JSP Strategic Objective 1.2 (Defeat ISIS, al-Qa'ida and other transnational terrorist organizations, and counter state-sponsored, regional, and local terrorist groups that threaten U.S. national security interests) by reducing regional and local vulnerabilities and increasing the ability of communities to respond to the presence of VEOs.

Délégitimer le recours à la terreur en cherchant à mettre en évidence l'immoralité fondamentale, les coûts et les impacts négatifs du recours à la violence et à souligner les avantages du recours à des alternatives pacifiques et tolérantes.

(USAID Région Afrique de l'Ouest) : L'USAID soutiendra le développement des médias, les communications stratégiques et les activités de changement d'attitude dans le cadre de l'effort plus large de l'USAID pour lutter contre l'extrémisme violent (CVE) au Sahel. Les activités de l'exercice 2019 comprendront : La diffusion de feuilletons radiophoniques et d'émissions interactives dans plusieurs langues locales, atteignant une audience quotidienne estimée à 3 millions d'auditeurs. L'élargissement de la portée et le renforcement des capacités de 80 stations de radio communautaires locales partenaires grâce à une formation technique, une formation en gestion et un soutien en équipement. . ..Un essai contrôlé randomisé a démontré que l’écoute d’un feuilleton radiophonique financé par l’USAID sur CVE entraînait une augmentation significative (18 %) de la probabilité de citer la collaboration avec les forces de sécurité comme une stratégie clé pour lutter contre l’extrémisme violent. Grâce à cette activité et à d’autres, Voices for Peace (V4P) fait progresser les pays sur la voie de l’autonomie en renforçant l’engagement des communautés en faveur de la lutte contre l’extrémisme violent et en augmentant la capacité des gouvernements et des acteurs de la société civile à travailler au sein des communautés, répondant ainsi aux griefs généralement exploités par les organisations d’extrémisme violent (OEV). V4P travaille actuellement à travers le Sahel et cible les régions où VEO est présent. V4P défend les intérêts de sécurité nationale des États-Unis en empêchant la propagation de groupes extrémistes violents qui cherchent à nuire aux Américains dans le pays et à l’étranger. Cette activité contribue directement à l'objectif stratégique 1.2 du JSP (Vaincre l'Etat islamique, Al-Qaïda et d'autres organisations terroristes transnationales, et contrer les groupes terroristes parrainés par l'État, régionaux et locaux qui menacent les intérêts de sécurité nationale des États-Unis) en réduisant les vulnérabilités régionales et locales et en augmentant la capacité des communautés à répondre à la présence d'OEV.

description.narrative: The Ending AIDS in West Africa project helps to meet the 90-90-90 targets to end the AIDS epidemic, outlined by the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS), through a focus on tailored HIV testing, treatment and care services for key populations in the region, particularly sex workers and men who have sex with men. FHI 360 and core project partners, Johns Hopkins University and Enda Sant, design programming that is informed by existing, high-impact practices based on past successes and identified gaps and by new evidence and best practices from the global key population community of practice. Ending AIDS in West Africa is a five-year technical assistance project funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development. The project is establishing eight key population centers of excellence in Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Cte dIvoire, Guinea and Togo to provide appropriate programming, amplify efforts, serve as training hubs and sustain services beyond the life of the project. Leveraging existing multisectoral partnerships, the centers deliver services through a differentiated model of care approach that tailors activities to people and groups. It connects people to share their experiences, access information and classes, and rapidly exchange best practices and innovations.

Le projet Mettre fin au sida en Afrique de l'Ouest contribue à atteindre les objectifs 90-90-90 pour mettre fin à l'épidémie de sida, définis par le Programme commun des Nations Unies sur le VIH/sida (ONUSIDA), en mettant l'accent sur des services adaptés de dépistage, de traitement et de soins du VIH pour les populations clés de la région, en particulier les professionnel(le)s du sexe et les hommes ayant des rapports sexuels avec des hommes. FHI 360 et les principaux partenaires du projet, l'Université Johns Hopkins et Enda Sant, conçoivent des programmes qui s'appuient sur des pratiques existantes à fort impact basées sur les succès passés et les lacunes identifiées, ainsi que sur de nouvelles preuves et meilleures pratiques de la communauté de pratique mondiale des populations clés. Mettre fin au sida en Afrique de l'Ouest est un projet d'assistance technique de cinq ans financé par l'Agence américaine pour le développement international. Le projet établit huit centres d'excellence pour les populations clés au Bénin, au Burkina Faso, au Cameroun, en Côte d'Ivoire, en Guinée et au Togo pour fournir des programmes appropriés, amplifier les efforts, servir de centres de formation et maintenir les services au-delà de la durée de vie du projet. Tirant parti des partenariats multisectoriels existants, les centres fournissent des services selon un modèle d'approche de soins différencié qui adapte les activités aux personnes et aux groupes. Il connecte les gens pour partager leurs expériences, accéder à des informations et à des cours, et échanger rapidement les meilleures pratiques et innovations.

Le projet Mettre fin au sida en Afrique de l'Ouest contribue à atteindre les objectifs 90-90-90 pour mettre fin à l'épidémie de sida, définis par le Programme commun des Nations Unies sur le VIH/sida (ONUSIDA), en mettant l'accent sur des services adaptés de dépistage, de traitement et de soins du VIH pour les populations clés de la région, en particulier les professionnel(le)s du sexe et les hommes ayant des rapports sexuels avec des hommes. FHI 360 et les principaux partenaires du projet, l'Université Johns Hopkins et Enda Sant, conçoivent des programmes qui s'appuient sur des pratiques existantes à fort impact basées sur les succès passés et les lacunes identifiées, ainsi que sur de nouvelles preuves et meilleures pratiques de la communauté de pratique mondiale des populations clés. Mettre fin au sida en Afrique de l'Ouest est un projet d'assistance technique de cinq ans financé par l'Agence américaine pour le développement international. Le projet établit huit centres d'excellence pour les populations clés au Bénin, au Burkina Faso, au Cameroun, en Côte d'Ivoire, en Guinée et au Togo pour fournir des programmes appropriés, amplifier les efforts, servir de centres de formation et maintenir les services au-delà de la durée de vie du projet. Tirant parti des partenariats multisectoriels existants, les centres fournissent des services selon un modèle d'approche de soins différencié qui adapte les activités aux personnes et aux groupes. Il connecte les gens pour partager leurs expériences, accéder à des informations et à des cours, et échanger rapidement les meilleures pratiques et innovations.

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): The West African Health Organization (WAHO) is a regional institution with the mandate to coordinate and harmonize health policies across the 15 member states of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). In line with USAID Forward reform, USAID/West Africa will support WAHO to strengthen its capacity to lead health efforts in the region. FY 2014 funds will support: strategic planning to align WAHO with the ECOWAS planning process; operationalizing WAHO's health information policy in the 15 member states; operationalizing WAHO's advocacy and communications strategies; continuing a regional forum for best practices in health in West Africa; developing a strategy to engage the private sector on mobile health; strengthening partnerships with other African institutions such as the East, Central and Southern African Community Health Community and the African Union; and exploring a regional platform for maternal and neonatal death review, surveillance and response.

description.narrative: (USAID West Africa Regional): USAID implements a variety of peace-building and governance activities, including both regional programs and bilateral activities in USAID non-presence countries. This presents USAID with a broad and complex portfolio where outcome and impact measurement can be difficult. Monitoring and evaluation challenges are compounded by the low capacity of many local organizations to effectively design and implement the collection of field data. In some instances, poor quality work has undermined or limited the value of monitoring and evaluation plans. The broad and varied nature of activities covered by RPGO also presents potential opportunities for cross-country or cross-program/-sectoral learning that can be enhanced through improved evaluation. To address these issues, the Evaluation and Analytical Services project will facilitate improved analysis of the impact of regional peace-building and governance interventions through more rigorous measurement and systematic documentation of results. It will provide a management tool for cross-country, cross-sectoral and cross-program learning and for future designs while also serving to upgrade local capacity for evaluation services. In sum, the objective of this activity is to increase the availability of quality information in the region in a manner that can support improved achievement of development objectives and can be sustained after the end of the contract period.
